work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: To all that fear God in the Burrough and Parish of Kederminster in Worcestershire.

items.text: Do not silence yourself from instructing and praying with your household; this is your work.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, To all that fear God in the Burrough and Parish of Kederminster in Worcestershire
items.quote: O that the Rulers of Families... did not silence themselves, from that Instructing, and Prayer which is their work?

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. … § 4

items.text: Obey your parents' peremptory command to marry when you are under their power and no greater matter hinders, for their command signifies God's command.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Christian Oeconomicks, Chap. 1 §4
items.quote: the command of Parents signifieth the command of God

items.text: Do not causelessly refuse your parents' desires when they persuade you concerning marriage.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Christian Oeconomicks, Chap. 1 §4
items.quote: their desires must not be causlesly refused

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Title Page

items.text: Serve the Lord with your whole household.
items.quote: But as for Me and my House, we will serve the Lord.

items.text: Teach God's words diligently to your children, and talk of them throughout the day.
items.quote: thou shalt teach them diligently to thy Children, and thou shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy House...

items.text: Do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
items.quote: Ye Fathers provoke not your Children to wrath, but bring them up in the Nurture and Admonition of the Lord.

items.text: Let your household be a God-fearing household, given to prayer and alms.
items.quote: Cornelius—a devout man, and One that feared God with all his House; which gave much Alms to the people, and Prayed to God alwayes.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Join together as a household in prayer and solemn worship of God.
items.quote: families be to the utmost of their capacities devoted to God; and consequently that they solemnly worship him

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 5 … § 7

items.text: Obey your parents' command to marry when no greater reason stands against it; if they command it, let their will oblige you as a means to your ultimate end.
items.quote: the will of Parents alone may oblige you; if there be no greater thing against it

items.text: Do not marry when your parents absolutely forbid it, unless obeying them would clearly hinder your service to God and your salvation.
items.quote: Parents prohibitions may make it a sin, when there is a clear probability that it would most conduce to our ultimate end, were it not prohibited.

items.text: Do not command your child to marry or remain single against God or their salvation; you have no authority to command what would hinder their ultimate end.
items.quote: Parents have no authority to command you any thing against God or your salvation or your ultimate end.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Lead the household in stated, solemn worship of God, not leaving it to children or servants to do alone.
items.quote: twenty children, or servants shall worship God without the Father, or Master of the family either present himself, or in some Representative, it is not a family worship

items.text: When the head leads in worship, attend and mentally concur in his prayers and praise.
items.quote: the rest perform their parts by receiving instructions, or mentally concurring in the Prayers and praise by him put up.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 41

items.text: Make provision for your wife and children while you live, and leave provision for them after your death.
items.quote: some provision must be made for them when you are dead

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · Tit. 2. Cases of Marriage.

items.text: Keep your marriage covenant and all marriage duties; do not part without a necessary cause, even if you doubt the lawfulness of your degree of marriage.
items.quote: Marriage duties are certainly commanded to the married... Husband and Wife to break their Covenants and part, without a necessary cause is a great sin.

items.text: If you are married in a clearly forbidden degree, part as incestuous and do not continue in that state.
items.quote: they must part as incestuous, and not continue in a forbidden state

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 8 … § 12

items.text: Obey your parents' prohibition of marriage as long as you live under their government, especially in your younger years.
items.quote: it is necessary to obey them during the time that the Children live under the Government of their Parents

items.text: Do not marry against your parents' will, for their authority is given for your good, not your destruction.
items.quote: they have their Power to edification, and not unto destruction

items.text: When your parents forbid you to marry the person you are fond of, subdue that unruly affection and obey them.
items.quote: such fondness ... as will not stoop to reason and your Parents wills, is inordinate and sinful

items.text: Before marrying when your parents forbid, ask others to intercede and seek their consent.
items.quote: he is to procure some others to sollicite his Parents for their consent

items.text: If you have promised marriage and your parents oppose it, do not fulfill that promise while they remain opposed.
items.quote: such a child is bound to forbear the fullfilling of that promise till the Parents do consent or die

items.text: Do not marry another while that promise stands, unless the promised person releases you, for your parents may yet consent.
items.quote: he is bound from marrying any other (unless he be disobliged by the person)

items.text: Honor your parents' will in marriage even when grown and independent, but you are not bound to the same absolute obedience as in childhood.
items.quote: though we owe Parents a limited obedience still, yet at full age the Child is more at his own dispose than he was before

items.text: Use your authority over your children's marriage for their edification, and do not forbid marriage to their destruction.
items.quote: they have their Power to edification, and not unto destruction

items.text: Strive to avoid both disobedience to your parents and unchastity; if you cannot avoid both, choose the lesser evil of disobeying them rather than living in lust.
items.quote: it is the smaller sin to choose to disobey his Parents, rather than to live in the flames of lust

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 2 · Directions for the right choice of Servants and Masters. · Part 1 · PART I. Directions for the right choice of Servants.

items.text: Choose servants who are fit for the work: healthful, skilled in the work, and willing to labor.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 2, Part 1
items.quote: Three things are necessary to make a servant fit for you: 1. Strength, 2. Skill, 3. Willingness.

items.text: Choose servants who fear God, or at least are tractable and willing to be taught, not ungodly or profane.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 2, Part 1
items.quote: choose such as have the fear of God, or at least such as are tractable and willing to be taught, and not such as are ungodly, sensual and profane.

items.text: Judge a servant's godliness by his love of godliness and conscientious duty, not by his talk or knowledge.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 2, Part 1
items.quote: measure not the Godliness of a servant by his bare knowledge or words, but by his LOVE and CONSCIENCE.

items.text: If you must take an unfit or bad servant, carry yourself vigilantly and convincingly to make him better, remembering he has an immortal soul.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 2, Part 1
items.quote: carry your self towards them in a vigilant convincing manner, so as tendeth most to make them better.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 56 … § 58

items.text: Make and keep the marriage covenant with understanding, deliberation, and fixed resolution to be faithful.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 56
items.quote: Let your Marriage Covenant be made understandingly, deliberately, heartily, in the fear of God, with a fixed resolution faithfully to perform it.

items.text: Help each other on the way to the heavenly Jerusalem, that your journey may be easier and you may meet again there.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 58
items.quote: help each other in your way, that your journey may be the easier to you, and that you may happily meet again in the Heavenly Hierusalem.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Worship God solemnly together as a household, using the opportunities and advantages he has given you for his glory.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 3
items.quote: Families, having such Advantages and opportunities for Gods solemn Worship, are bound to improve them faithfully for God, in the solemn worshipping of him.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 34 … § 40

items.text: Teach your children the doctrine of salvation; talk of God's word diligently at home and abroad, when you sit and when you walk, when you lie down and when you rise.
items.quote: teach his word diligently ... unto their children

items.text: Root out the corruptions in your children's hearts by all possible diligence.
items.quote: What abundance of obstinate rooted corruptions are in the hearts of Children which Parents must by all possible diligence root up?

items.text: Teach your servants the matters of their salvation, and mind them of it, as part of your duty over them.
items.quote: so great is your duty in teaching them, and minding them of the matters of their salvation

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 49 … § 55

items.text: Refuse to obey your parents when they command you to marry an ungodly person, for God has forbidden it.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, ch.1, §50
items.quote: God having forbidden it, no Parent hath authority to command you to do so great a mischief to your self

items.text: Be a faithful friend: share your mind, assist in affairs, bear burdens, comfort in sorrows, and be a daily companion.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, ch.1, §55
items.quote: a faithful friend, that loveth you entirely, and is as true to you as your self, to whom you may open your mind and communicate your affairs

items.text: Join in prayer and holy exercises, watch over each other's souls, tell each other of sins and dangers, and stir up God's grace.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, ch.1, §55
items.quote: to joyn with you in prayer and other holy exercises; to watch over you and tell you of your sins and dangers, and to stir up in you the grace of God

items.text: Do not be wanting in your duty to bring up a godly seed; for this is the end of marriage.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, ch.1, §55
items.quote: It is no small mercy to be the Parents of a Godly seed: and this is the end of the institution of marriage

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 18 … § 26

items.text: Provide food and clothing for your children.
items.quote: a Father that had vowed never to provide food or rayment for his children

items.text: Give mutual help and comfort to one another in marriage.
items.quote: other lawful ends of marriage, as mutual help and comfort

items.text: Provide food, drink, and clothing for your household, taking thought for their needs.
items.quote: what you shall eat, and what you shall drink, and wherewith shall you and yours be cloathed?

items.text: Provide for your children, even after your death, laying up for those who survive you.
items.quote: you must provide for children that survive you

items.text: Provide for your wife and children before giving to charitable uses.
items.quote: Wife and Children are provided for

items.text: Educate your children piously for God's service.
items.quote: educate your own Children piously for his service

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 27 … § 33

items.text: Bear patiently with her weaknesses and infirmities, as with a weaker vessel.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 27
items.quote: it is no small patience which the natural imbecility of the female sex requireth you to prepare.

items.text: Bear one another's faults and imperfections, and do not provoke each other to anger or passion.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 28
items.quote: there is such a meeting of faults and imperfections on both sides, that maketh it much the harder to bear the infirmities of others aright.

items.text: Instruct one another in the ways of God.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: As to instruct, admonish, pray, watch over one another, and to be continual helpers to each other in order to their everlasting happiness.

items.text: Admonish one another when either goes astray.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: As to instruct, admonish, pray, watch over one another, and to be continual helpers to each other in order to their everlasting happiness.

items.text: Pray for one another's spiritual good.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: As to instruct, admonish, pray, watch over one another, and to be continual helpers to each other in order to their everlasting happiness.

items.text: Watch over one another's souls, that you may both attain everlasting happiness.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: As to instruct, admonish, pray, watch over one another, and to be continual helpers to each other in order to their everlasting happiness.

items.text: Be continual helpers to each other in the way of salvation.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: As to instruct, admonish, pray, watch over one another, and to be continual helpers to each other in order to their everlasting happiness.

items.text: Patiently bear with the infirmities of each other.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 32
items.quote: patiently to bear with the infirmities of each other.

items.text: Share in each other's griefs and bear one another's burdens.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 33
items.quote: the more they Love each other, the more they participate in each others griefs.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Teach your household the word of God, reading the Scriptures and instructing them in his ways.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Rulers must teach their families the word of God

items.text: Pray with your household, asking God's blessing on the reading and instruction.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: If Rulers must teach their families the word of God, then must they pray with them

items.text: Teach your household to pray, and lead them in prayer before God.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: If Rulers of families are bound to teach their families to Pray, then are they bound to Pray with them

items.text: Lead your family in solemn prayer and praise to God, as a church.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: All Churches ought solemnly to pray to God and praise him. A Christian family is a Church.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God. · Objections answered.

items.text: Lead your household in prayer: be their mouth to God in family worship; use a form rather than omit it if you cannot pray without one.
items.quote: use a Book or form, rather than not to pray in their families at all

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Provide for your own household: food, clothing, and all necessary provision, for he who does not provide for his own has denied the faith.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: He that provideth not for his own, especially those of his houshold, hath denied the faith, and is worse than an Infidel.

items.text: As head of the house, see that all in your household join together in worship, especially in prayer and praise.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: If God hath given charge to the Ruler of the Family to see that the rest do worship him in that Family.

items.text: Require and oversee that your household sanctify the Lord's Day, for the fourth commandment includes your sons, daughters, and servants.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: The fourth Commandment requireth the Ruler of the Family... that his Son and Daughter, and Man servant and Maid servant... should do it.

items.text: Join with the household in common prayer and praise when the head leads, so that he may see that you worship God.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: the Ruler may be satisfied... to see that they all joyn in Prayer

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · Tit. 2. Cases of Marriage.

items.text: Do not impose vows of chastity or other oaths on your children, or induce them to make such vows.
items.quote: If Parents or others impose such Oaths and Vows on their Children or Subjects, or induce them to it, it is sinfully done of them

items.text: Exercise the care and power over your children's marriage that God has committed to you.
items.quote: It is Parents that God hath committed more of this care and power to, about Childrens Marriage, than to Princes.

items.text: Do not command your children to break a lawful vow unless they are already released from it.
items.quote: Parents nor Princes may not lawfully command the breach of such a Vow, (not nullified at first,) except in such cases as disoblige us whether they do it or not

items.text: Obey your parents' just commands about marriage.
items.quote: When Parents or Princes may justly command it, we may justly obey them.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Lead your household in prayer and praise as one in a priestly role, serving God together.
items.quote: Every Ruler of a family then was as a Priest to his own family.

items.text: Train your children in the worship of God and guide them in it.
items.quote: a training them up in the Worship of God, and guiding them therein.

items.text: Rule your children well, keeping them in subjection with all gravity.
items.quote: having his children in subjection, with all gravity.

items.text: Join together as a household in prayer, confessing shared sins and giving thanks for shared mercies.
items.quote: they often so sin together, as maketh it fit that they confess and lament it together: and some mercies which they receive together, its fit they seek, and give thanks for together.

items.text: Stay united with the household in prayer; do not separate to pray only in secret.
items.quote: it is a kind of Family-schism, in such cases to separate from one another, and to pray in secret only.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Obey your master as unto Christ, and serve him as serving the Lord Christ.
items.quote: Servants must be obedient unto their Masters as unto Christ, and serve them as serving the Lord Christ

items.text: Teach and admonish every member of your household in the Word of God, as one who speaks the oracles of God.
items.quote: Much more must the Rulers of families do so to Wives, Children and Servants

items.text: Rule your children well, governing them in the things of God and salvation, as a man who would rule the church.
items.quote: Those that are to be chosen Deacons or Bishops must be such as Rule their own Children and their own houshold well

items.text: Rule your own household well in religious holy governing, that you may be fit to rule the church of God.
items.quote: If a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he rule the Church of God?

items.text: Do not receive into your house anyone who does not bring the doctrine of Christ, and do not bid him Godspeed.
items.quote: If there come any to you and bring not this Doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed

items.text: Correct your children, using corporal or sensible punishment or withdrawing benefits, as Scripture requires; do not neglect it as Eli did.
items.quote: The Duty of correcting either by corporal sensible punishment or by withdrawing some benefit

items.text: Do not allow a lying or deceitful servant to dwell in your house; put away the wicked from your household.
items.quote: He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house, he that telleth lyes shall not tarry in my sight.

items.text: Lead your family in solemn prayer and praise to God, taking the fit opportunities you have together.
items.quote: Solemn Prayer and praises of God in and by Christian families is of Divine appointment.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 2 · Directions for the right choice of Servants and Masters. · Part 2 · PART II. Directions for the right choice of Masters.

items.text: Care for your servants' souls as well as their bodies: teach them to know God, hinder them from sin, and help them prepare for salvation.
items.quote: A Master that feareth God, will help to save you from sin and Hell, and help your souls to life eternal: He will hinder you from sin: he will teach you to know God, and to prepare for your salvation.

items.text: Do your servants no wrong, but love them as Christians and fellow servants of Christ while you command them.
items.quote: A Master that feareth God will do you no wrong, but will love you as a Christian, and his fellow servant of Christ, while he commandeth and employeth you as his own servant.

items.text: Labor diligently, be trustworthy, obedient, gentle, and patient; excel in virtue so that you may be a good servant.
items.quote: Excel others in labour, and diligence, and trustiness, and obedience, and gentleness, and patience, and then you may have almost what places you desire.

items.text: Give your servants the wages and respect that their work and virtues deserve.
items.quote: they owe you nothing but what your work and virtues shall deserve.

items.text: Do not by idle, frothy talk, derision of holiness, or bad example blot out godly instruction; encourage one another by good discourse and practice.
items.quote: the idle frothy talk of fellow-servants may blot out all from your memories and hearts. And their derision of a holy life, or their bad examples, may do more hurt.

items.text: So order the work that your servants may have time for prayer, Scripture reading, and care of their souls, and do not overburden them.
items.quote: A service which alloweth you no time at all to pray, or read the Scripture, or mind your everlasting state, is a life more fit for beasts than men.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Improve your interest, power, and parts to bring your whole family to Christ and dedicate them to God.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: to improve his interest, power, and parts to the uttermost, to bring all his family to be the people of Christ in the Baptismal Covenant, and so to dedicate all his family to Christ.

items.text: Love your wife with a holy love in the Lord, as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Husbands must love their Wives with an Holy Love in the Lord, even as the Lord loved the Church, who gave himself for it, to sanctifie and cleanse it

items.text: Submit to your husband as unto the Lord, as the church is subject to Christ.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Wives must submit themselves to their Husbands as unto the Lord; and be subject to them, as the Church is to Christ

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Children must obey their Parents in the Lord

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Parents must bring up their children in the Nurture and Admonition of the Lord

items.text: Obey your masters as unto Christ, doing service as to the Lord, not to man.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Servants must be obedient unto their Masters as unto Christ, and as the servants of Christ, doing service as to the Lord, and not to man

items.text: Do the same to them, knowing that your Master is in heaven.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: Masters must do the same to them, knowing that their Master is in Heaven

items.text: Teach all under your authority the doctrine of salvation and the terms on which it is to be had.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3
items.quote: It is the Will of God that the Rulers of families should teach those that are under them the Doctrine of salvation

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 42 … § 44

items.text: Prepare yourself with marriage strength and patience for the duties and sufferings of a married state before entering it.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: See that you be furnished with Marriage-strength and patience, for the duties and sufferings of a married state, before you venture on it.

items.text: Love your spouse with rational, justified love, not blind fancy or lust.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 43
items.quote: that Love must be Rational, and such as you can justifie in the severest tryal, by the evidences of worth and fitness

items.text: Bear with your spouse's infirmities and endure the daily crosses of married life patiently.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: See that you are well provided with Marriage-patience; to beat with the infirmities of others, and undergo the daily crosses of your life

items.text: Remain constant in the love and resolutions that brought you into marriage, continuing to the last.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: Let the Love and Resolutions which brought you into that state, continue with you to the last.

items.text: Instruct and edify your household, and live with them as one having knowledge.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: that you may be able to instruct and edifie your families, and may live with them as men of knowledge

items.text: Be diligent in the duties of married life, answering to their greatness.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: See that you be provided with a diligence answerable to the greatness of your undertaken duties.

items.text: Cherish conjugal affection for your spouse, as necessary for the duties and sufferings of married life.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 1, § 42
items.quote: See that you be well provided with Conjugal affections: For they are necessary both to the Duties and Sufferings of a married life

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Command all under you in the worship of God, and inflict penalties on children and servants who refuse.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3, Argument 1
items.quote: he may command all that are under him in God Worship, yea, and may inflict penalties on children and servants that refuse

items.text: Use your singular interest in your wife and children to bring them willingly to family worship.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3, Argument 1
items.quote: He hath the Advantage of a singular Interest in Wife and Children by which he may bring them to it willingly

items.text: Fit your reproofs, exhortations, confessions, and petitions to the particular spiritual needs of each family member.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3, Argument 1
items.quote: the Ruler, by familiarity and daily converse, is enabled more particularly to fit his reproofs and exhortations confessions and petitions accordingly

items.text: Help one another serve God and further one another's salvation.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3, Argument 1
items.quote: Being nearest in Relation, they are stronglier obliged to further each others salvation, and help each other in serving God

items.text: Obey the head of the family when he commands you to worship God, and accept discipline if you refuse.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 3, Argument 1
items.quote: he may command all that are under him in God Worship, yea, and may inflict penalties on children and servants that refuse

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 45 … § 48

items.text: Do not be hasty in choosing a spouse; deliberate well and thoroughly know the person on whom so much of your comfort or sorrow will depend.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 1, §45
items.quote: Be not too hasty in your choice or resolution, but deliberate well, and throughly know the person

items.text: Let no carnal motives persuade you to marry an ungodly person; prefer the holy fear of God before all worldly excellency.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 1, §46
items.quote: Let no carnal motives perswade you to joyn your self to an ungodly person; but let the holy fear of God be preferred in your choice before all worldly excellency whatsoever.

items.text: Do not be unequally yoked with an unbeliever; do not marry one who does not share your faith.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 1, §48
items.quote: Be ye not unequally yoaked together with unbelievers

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Pray together in the family, not only alone in secret.
items.quote: for a family to have access to God in joynt prayers and praises, is a mercy that God offereth them

items.text: Sing psalms and spiritual songs together as a family.
items.quote: singing of Psalms which I before proved an ordinary Duty of conjunct Christians, Therefore of families.

items.text: Teach and admonish one another in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs.
items.quote: Teaching and admonishing one another in Psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts unto the Lord.

items.text: Prefer joint family prayer over private prayer alone.
items.quote: They still ought to prefer conjunct prayer.

items.text: Lead joint prayer as the tongue of the family, speaking for the whole household.
items.quote: the tongue of the Church, and of the family must speak for the whole body

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 6 · More special Motives for a holy and careful Education of Children. · § 9

items.text: Give them a holy and careful education: instruct them diligently in the faith, watch over their souls, and correct them when needed.
items.quote: Educate them then and use them as men for the Love and Obedience of their Maker.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God. · Of the frequency and seasons of Family-Worship.

items.text: Lead the household in prayer and thanksgiving every morning and evening.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Oeconomicks, Ch. 3, Of the frequency and seasons of Family-Worship
items.quote: Ordinarily it should be every day and twice a day: and the Morning and Evening are ordinarily the fitest seasons.

items.text: Teach children God's word and pray with them when they lie down and rise up.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Oeconomicks, Ch. 3, Of the frequency and seasons of Family-Worship
items.quote: Parents teach their Children the Word of God when they lye down, and when they rise up: ... pray with them lying down and rising up.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 1 · A Christian Directory. TOM. II. Christian Oeconomicks. CHAP. I. Directions about Marriage; for Choice and Contract. · § 13 … § 17

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent; if you have promised to do so, do not fulfill that promise until it becomes lawful by their consent.
items.quote: If... the matter Promised (as is marrying without Parents consent,) then it must be repented of, and not performed till it become lawful.

items.text: Keep your promise to marry: your promise binds you, but fulfill it only when lawful, that is, after your parents' consent.
items.quote: they can oblige themselves to God or man

items.text: Live together as husband and wife even if you married without your parents' consent; your marriage is valid and must continue.
items.quote: such Marriage is valid, and to be continued though it was sinfully made

items.text: Do not forbid your married child to live with his or her spouse; you have no authority to dissolve their marriage.
items.quote: Parents cannot forbid Husband and Wife to live together

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 4 · General Directions for the Holy Government of Families. · § 20

items.text: As much as possible, settle a constant order for all your affairs, so that every ordinary work has its time and confusion does not shut out godliness.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 4 · General Directions for the Holy Government of Families. · § 20
items.quote: settle a constant order of all your businesses, that every ordinary work may know its time, and confusion may not shut out Godliness

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 5 · Special Motives to perswade men to the Holy Governing of their Families. · § 3 … § 4

items.text: Govern your household so that God's law is the chief rule, the Scriptures are daily opened, God is praised and called upon, and all speak as those bound for heaven.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5 § 3
items.quote: where Gods Law is the principal Rule, and where you may be daily taught the mysteries of his Kingdom, and have the Scriptures opened to you

items.text: Train up children for God betimes, before sin takes deep root, by wise and holy education.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5 § 4
items.quote: no means in all the world, doth more effectually tend to the happiness of souls, than wise and holy education

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Teach your children to pray and praise God, and pray with them or in their hearing so they learn by practice.
items.quote: They are bound to bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord... therefore to teach them to Pray and Praise God

items.text: Teach your servants to pray by praying with them and before them.
items.quote: They are cruel to Children and Servants that teach them not to pray by practice and example.

items.text: Lead the household to give thanks to God together at meals, that the food may be sanctified.
items.quote: If families must with thanksgiving receive their meat as from God... They eat together: therefore they must give thanks together.

items.text: Dwell with her according to knowledge and honor, and join together with her in prayer, so that your prayers are not hindered.
items.quote: dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour to the Wife... that your prayers be not hindered... conjunct prayer of Husband and Wife being proved a duty

items.text: Admonish one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
items.quote: teaching and admonishing one another in Psalms and Hymns and spiritual Songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.

items.text: Do all things in word and deed in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
items.quote: whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Iesus; giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

items.text: Offer regular family prayer in the house, as Daniel did three times a day, even when it endangers your life.
items.quote: he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God

items.text: Commit your household to serve the Lord, and lead them in his service.
items.quote: as for me and my house we will serve the Lord.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 5 · Special Motives to perswade men to the Holy Governing of their Families. · § 9 … § 11

items.text: Govern your household in holiness and order, and do not be negligent, for such negligence corrupts children and servants and causes much sin.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, §11
items.quote: the sinful negligence of Parents and Masters in their families, is as great, if not much greater than that.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Devote your house to the Lord and lead them in his worship, for your family is a society sanctified to him.
items.quote: Josh. (24.) devoteth himself and his house to the Lord: I and my house will serve the Lord.

items.text: Consecrate your children to God, as Abraham consecrated his household by circumcision.
items.quote: Abraham by Circumcision (the Covenant or seal of the Covenant of God) consecrated his whole houshold to God

items.text: Honor your father, for not to honor him is contemptuous and disobedient.
items.quote: If one of you had a Son that were blind, and could not see his own Father, would you think him therefore excusable, if he would not honour his Father

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 6 · More special Motives for a holy and careful Education of Children. · § 3 … § 4

items.text: Bring them up virtuously to lead a godly and Christian life, as you solemnly promised at their baptism.
items.quote: bring them up vertuously to lead a godly and Christian life

items.text: Teach them diligently the doctrine of God's holy word from childhood; it is God's first appointed means for their faith.
items.quote: Parents diligently to teach their children the doctrine of his holy Word

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 6 … § 7

items.text: Take delight in the love and company and converse of each other.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: Husband and wife must take Delight in the Love and Company and converse of each other.

items.text: Avoid all things that may represent you unpleasant or unlovely to each other.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: Avoid therefore all things that may represent you unpleasant or unlovely to each other.

items.text: Use all lawful means to cherish complacency and delight.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: use all lawful means to cherish complacency and delight

items.text: Shun nastiness, uncleanness, unseemly carriage, and foolish speech that would hinder love and pleasure.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: Nastiness and uncleanness and unseemly carriage, and foolish speech, and whatever is loathsome in body or mind, must be shunned

items.text: Even in deformity or loathsome sickness, continue to love each other and take pleasure in converse.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: If there be any deformity of the body, or any thing unseemly in behaviour, or if God should visit them with any loathsom sores or sickness, they must for all that love each other

items.text: Do not turn away from your spouse in time of affliction, for you are one flesh.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: not turn away in time of her affliction, from her that is become his flesh

items.text: Do not be weary of each other's company or prefer the company of neighbors or strangers.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §6
items.quote: are weary of the company of one another, and had rather be in their Neighbours houses than in their own

items.text: Live in quietness and peace, and avoid all occasions of wrath and discord.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 7, §7
items.quote: It is a great duty of Husbands and Wives to live in quietness and peace, and avoid all occasions of wrath and discord.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 5 · Special Motives to perswade men to the Holy Governing of their Families. · § 5 … § 8

items.text: Teach and catechize your children at home, preparing them to understand and love the doctrine of the church.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, § 5
items.quote: Catechizing them in the Church, which should have been done at home.

items.text: Give your children a holy education, so that they may become good magistrates and good subjects.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, § 6
items.quote: A good education is the first and greatest work to make good Magistrates and good Subjects.

items.text: Lead your household in prayer, instruction, holy conversation, and discipline, especially when public worship is restricted.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, § 7
items.quote: Christian Families are called Churches, because they consist of holy persons, that worship God, and learn, and love, and obey his word.

items.text: Govern and teach your own family diligently and without fear, for it is your unquestionable charge and duty.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, § 8
items.quote: Your own house is your Castle: Your family is your charge: You may teach them as oft and as diligently as you will.

items.text: Be subject to your parents, learning obedience to them as preparation for subjection to God and to lawful superiors.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 5, § 6
items.quote: have first learnt to be subject to God, and to their Parents.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 10 … § 13

items.text: Help her in the knowledge and worship and obedience of God for her salvation, with special care and diligence.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 7, §10
items.quote: help each other in the knowledge and worship and obedience of God in order to their salvation.

items.text: Help him in the knowledge and worship and obedience of God for his salvation, with special care and diligence.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 7, §10
items.quote: help each other in the knowledge and worship and obedience of God in order to their salvation.

items.text: Love her as Christ loved the church and gave himself for it, that he might sanctify and cleanse her.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 7, §13
items.quote: husbands must love their Wives as Christ loved his Church, who gave himself for it that he might sanctifie it and cleanse it

items.text: Do not hinder her holiness and salvation; instead be a helper to her soul.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 7, §12
items.quote: are hinderers of the holiness and salvation of each other

items.text: Do not hinder his holiness and salvation; instead be a helper to his soul.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 7, §12
items.quote: are hinderers of the holiness and salvation of each other

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 6 · More special Motives for a holy and careful Education of Children. · § 5

items.text: Use all the advantages God has given you to be an instrument of your children's good and to promote their salvation.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: By all these advantages God hath enabled you above all others, to be instruments of your Childrens good, and the first and greatest promoters of their salvation.

items.text: Begin instruction early, before false opinions and bad impressions take root, and make the first impressions on their tender hearts.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: You have them in hand betime, before they have received any false opinions, or bad impressions... You are to make the first impressions upon them.

items.text: Use the rod of correction to drive foolishness from your child.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child, but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

items.text: Watch over your children and discern their faults early, that you may apply the best remedy.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: You have opportunity of watching over them, and discerning all their faults in time... for the choosing and applying of the best remedy.

items.text: Instruct them in a familiar manner, quickening their attention by questions.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: You have opportunity of speaking to them in the most familiar manner... You can quicken their attention by questions which put them upon answering you.

items.text: Repeat your instructions and press them home, so that what is not learned at one time may be learned at another.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: You can repeat your instructions, and drive them home, that what is not done at one time, may be done at another.

items.text: Place your children under the best means of grace and remove hindrances to their good.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: You have power to place them under the best means, and to remove many impediments out of their way.

items.text: Let your example be a continual and powerful sermon before your children.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: Your example is near them and continually in their sight, which is a continual and powerful Sermon.

items.text: Obey and honor your parents, for their authority is from God and unquestionable.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 6, § 5
items.quote: Your authority over your children is most unquestionable... Father and Mother as the first Natural Power, are mentioned rather than Kings or Queens in the fifth Commandment.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 6 · More special Motives for a holy and careful Education of Children. · § 6 … § 8

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, teaching them to know, love, and serve God, that you may hope they are his children.
items.quote: brought to know him, and love, and serve him, through your own endeavours in a pious education of them.

items.text: Love them with a spiritual love, as those that bear God's image, and not merely with natural affection.
items.quote: You may love your children upon an higher account than as they are yours: even as they are Gods, adorned with his Image

items.text: Provide for their bodily needs, doing your duty as their parent, while trusting God to care for them.
items.quote: though he will have you also do your duty for them, as they are your children.

items.text: Love your parents even when they have no more to give you.
items.quote: It will teach them to Love you, even when you have no more to give them

items.text: Honour your parents even if they are poor and contemptible in the eyes of others.
items.quote: It will teach them to honour you, though you are poor and contemptible in the eyes of others.

items.text: Obey your parents.
items.quote: It will teach them to obey you

items.text: Relieve your parents in want according to your power.
items.quote: and if you fall into want to relieve you according to their power

items.text: Comfort your parents in sickness and distress.
items.quote: It will fit them to comfort you in the time of your sickness and distress

items.text: Bear with your parents' weaknesses.
items.quote: A gracious child will bear with your weaknesses

items.text: Pray for and with your parents, and be a blessing to their house.
items.quote: A gracious Child can pray for you, and pray with you, and be a blessing to your house

items.text: Since you have conveyed original sin to them, do your best to save them by holy education.
items.quote: in justice you that have undone them, are bound to do your best to save them

items.text: Use the utmost wisdom and diligence in teaching and watching over them, for their sins are deep-rooted and not easily cast out.
items.quote: All the teaching, and diligence; and watchfulness that you can use, is little enough... They are obstinate vices that have possessed them

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 8

items.text: Keep up your conjugal love in constant heat and vigor toward your spouse, so that love suppresses wrath and heals any breach.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Keep up your conjugal Love in a constant heat and vigour. Love will suppress wrath

items.text: Mortify your pride and passion, and pray and labor for a humble, meek, and quiet spirit, for it is the diseased temper of the heart that causes dissensions.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: must mortifie their Pride and Passion which are the causes of Impatiency; and must pray and labour for a Humble, meek and quiet spirit.

items.text: Bear with your spouse's infirmities, remembering that you married a sinful, frail, imperfect person, not an angel or a blameless one.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Resolve therefore to bear with one another; as remembring that you took one another as sinful, frail, imperfect persons, and not as Angels

items.text: Remember that you are one flesh and be no more offended with your spouse's failings than you would be with your own; turn anger into compassion and seek cure.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Remember still that you are one flesh; and therefore be no more offended with the words or failings of each other, than you would be if they were your own

items.text: Agree beforehand that when one is in an angry fit, the other will silently and gently bear until it passes, and not answer wrath with wrath.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Agree together before hand, that when one is in the diseased angry fit, the other shall silently and gently bear, till it be past

items.text: Look before you and remember you must live together until death as companions and comforts; therefore do not disagree and vex each other.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Look before you, and remember that you must live together untill death, and must be the companions of each others fortunes, and the comforts of each others lives

items.text: As far as you are able, avoid all occasions of wrath about family matters; be diligent and skillful in managing your affairs so that they do not cause impatience.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: As far as you are able, avoid all occasions of wrath and falling out, about the matters of your Families

items.text: If you cannot quickly quench your passion, at least refrain your tongue from speaking reproachful or provoking words to your spouse.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: If you cannot quickly quench your passion, yet at least refrain your tongues: speak not reproachful or provoking words

items.text: Let the sober party condescend to speak fair and entreat the other with calm, gentle admonitions that revive reason.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Let the sober party condescend to speak fair and to intreat the other

items.text: When passion has prevailed, confess your fault to your spouse, ask forgiveness of each other, and join in prayer to God for pardon.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 7, § 8
items.quote: Confess your fault to one another, when passion hath prevailed against you; and ask forgiveness of each other, and joyn in prayer to God for pardon

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 3 · A DISPUTATION, OR, Arguments to prove the necessity of Family-worship and Holiness or Directions against the Cavils of the Prophane, and some Sectaries, who deny it to be a thing required by God.

items.text: Teach your children the word of God diligently, speaking of it at home and on the way, morning and night.
items.quote: you shall teach them your children, speaking of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down and when thou risest up

items.text: Command your children and household to keep the way of the Lord, using your authority as well as instruction.
items.quote: I know him that he will command his children and his houshold after him: and they shall keep the way of the Lord

items.text: Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, training them in the way they should go, feeding their souls as carefully as their bodies.
items.quote: Train up a child in the way where he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it. Bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord

items.text: Hear your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's law.
items.quote: My son hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother

items.text: Teach your wife the truths of God, so that she may be sanctified and cleansed by the word.
items.quote: Love your Wives as Christ loved the Church and gave himself for it, that he might sanctifie and cleanse it

items.text: Ask your husband at home for instruction, not speaking in the church.
items.quote: If they will learn any thing let them ask their husbands at home

items.text: Teach your household the plain necessary doctrines of the catechism and direct them in necessary practice, in subordination to the church's ministers.
items.quote: the master of the Family to let Controversies and obscure Scriptures alone, and to teach the plain few necessary Doctrines commonly contained in Catechisms

items.text: Hearken to your household head's teaching and learn from him, giving place to ministerial teaching when due.
items.quote: whatsoever proves it the Rulers Duty to teach must needs prove it the Families Duty to learn, and to hearken to his teaching

items.text: Do not hinder your family from attending the pastor's teaching; give place to him when he comes, and send your children and servants to be catechized when required.
items.quote: the Master is not then to be doing it himself, or to hinder them, but they must go first to the Pastor to be taught

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 1 … § 3

items.text: Love her with a true entire conjugal love, as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her, and as your own body.
items.quote: Husbands love your Wives, even as Christ also loved the Church, and gave himself for it... as their own bodies.

items.text: Love him with a true entire conjugal love.
items.quote: The first Duty of Husbands is to Love their Wives (and Wives their Husbands) with a true entire Conjugal Love.

items.text: Be willing and ready to succour one another for mutual help and comfort, as fellow-members.
items.quote: be as willing and ready to succour one another, as the hand is to help the eye or other fellow-member

items.text: Take more notice of the good in your wife than of the evil; do not let her faults make you forget her virtues.
items.quote: Take more notice of the good that is in your Wives, than of the evil.

items.text: Make not her infirmities to seem odious faults; excuse them as far as lawfully you may, considering her frailty and your own.
items.quote: Make not infirmities to seem odious faults, but excuse them as far as lawfully you may

items.text: Stir up what is best in her and not what is evil.
items.quote: Stir up that most in them into exercise which is best, and stir not up that which is evil

items.text: Overcome her with love, and by being a good husband make her a loving wife.
items.quote: Overcome them with Love... A good husband is the best means to make a good and loving Wife.

items.text: Set her an example of a prudent, lowly, loving, meek, self-denying, patient, harmless, holy, heavenly life.
items.quote: Give them examples of amiableness in your selves: set them the pattern of a prudent, lowly, loving, meek, self denying, patient, harmless, holy, heavenly life

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 14 … § 17

items.text: Be helpers to each other's souls, living together as heirs of heaven.
items.quote: live together as the heirs of Heaven, and to be helpers to each others souls.

items.text: Care for your own soul and feel the weight of eternal things, so that you can help your spouse's soul.
items.quote: you must each of you be sure that you have a care of your own: and retain a deep and lively apprehension of those great and everlasting matters

items.text: Take opportunities to speak seriously with each other about God and salvation, making these your greater business, with gravity and sobriety.
items.quote: Take those opportunities which your ordinary nearness and familiarity affordeth you, to be speaking seriously to each other about the matters of God and your salvation.

items.text: When your spouse speaks seriously about holy things, cherish the discourse by responding wisely or asking questions, and do not silence it by silence, contradiction, or diverting to worldly talk.
items.quote: let the other be careful to cherish, and not to extinguish and put an end to the discourse.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 4 · General Directions for the Holy Government of Families. · § 1 … § 9

items.text: Maintain your authority in your family, for if you lose it, your word will be of no effect.
items.quote: Let Governours maintain their Authority in their Families.

items.text: Rule over her only so far as necessary for household order, affairs, and comfortable cohabitation; let love and mutual interest do more than magisterial commands.
items.quote: Your Authority over your Wife, is but such as is necessary to the order of your Family, the safe and prudent management of your affairs, and your comfortable cohabitation.

items.text: Rule them with love, as is needed for their good education and felicity.
items.quote: Your authority over your Children is much greater: But yet only such as conjunct with Love, is needful to their good education and felicity.

items.text: Limit your authority over servants to what is agreed, for your service and God's honor.
items.quote: Your authority over your servants is to be measured by your contract with them... in order to your Service, and the honour of God.

items.text: Make your family understand that your authority is from God, and that in obeying you they obey him.
items.quote: Let your family understand that your Authority is of God, who is the God of Order, and that in obedience to him they are obliged to obey you.

items.text: Be holy and blameless, for sin makes you contemptible and holiness brings honor.
items.quote: The more of God appeareth upon you, in your knowledge and holiness and unblameableness of life, the greater will your Authority be.

items.text: Do not display weakness through passion or foolish speech or actions, lest you be despised.
items.quote: Shew not your natural weakness by passions, or imprudent words or deeds.

items.text: Use your authority, or your government will become a mere name.
items.quote: If you suffer Children and Servants but a little while to have the head, and to have, and say and do what they will, your Government will be but a name or image.

items.text: Keep a respectful distance; do not make children or servants your playfellows, or they will refuse your governance.
items.quote: If you make your children and servants your playfellows, or equals... they will quickly grow upon you... and will scorn to be subject where they have once been as equal.

items.text: Acquire prudence and skill to govern your household.
items.quote: Labour for Prudence and Skillfullness in Governing.

items.text: Teach your children the word of God, talking of it at home and abroad, lying down and rising up.
items.quote: all Parents must be able to teach it their children, and talk of it both at home and abroad, lying down and rising up.

items.text: Obey your household head, for his authority is from God and you obey God by obeying him.
items.quote: in obedience to him they are obliged to obey you.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 18 … § 24

items.text: Watch over the hearts and lives of one another, and labor to discern the state of each other's souls, sins, graces, and failings, so as to apply suitable help.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §18
items.quote: Watch over the hearts and lives of one another, and labour to discern the state of one anothers souls, and the strength or weakness of each others sins and graces.

items.text: When you reprove one another, do it in love, neither flattering away sins nor embittering the reproof with passion or contempt.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §19
items.quote: See that you neither flatter one another through fond and foolish love, nor exasperate one another by a passionate or contemptuous kind of reprehension.

items.text: Keep up true conjugal love, and do not grow disaffected with each other's persons, so that you may receive each other's counsel and reproof.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §20
items.quote: Be sure that you keep up true Conjugal love to one another, and that you grow not to disaffect the persons of each other.

items.text: Do not discourage each other from instruction and reproof by taking it ill, answering churlishly, or remaining obstinately unreformed.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §21
items.quote: Discourage not each other from instruction or reproof by taking it ill, or by churlish reflections, or by obstinate unreformedness.

items.text: Engage each other in reading edifying books, attending powerful preaching, and conversing with holy persons, while also giving your own help.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §22
items.quote: Engage each other in the reading of the most convincing quickning Books, and in attendance on the most powerful Ministry, and in profitable converse with the holiest persons.

items.text: Open the state of your souls and your faults to one another, for you are one flesh and need each other's help.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §23
items.quote: Conceal not the state of your souls, nor hide not your faults from one another.

items.text: Avoid contrariety of opinions in religion and sectarian divisions, lest you disaffect one another and hinder spiritual good.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 7, §24
items.quote: For if once you be of different judgements in matters which you take to be of great concernment, you will be tempted to disaffect, contemn or undervalue one another.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. … § 8

items.text: Love your husband specially, as your fitting return for all the trouble your infirmities put him to.
items.quote: Be specially loving to your Husbands

items.text: Submit to your husband as your head and governor, not merely in title but by following his understanding and will.
items.quote: Live in a voluntary subjection and obedience to them

items.text: Ask your husband for instruction when you need to learn, and do not rely on your own understanding.
items.quote: Learn of your Husbands as your appointed Teachers

items.text: Accept your husband's reproof and amend the faults he names; do not grudge at correction.
items.quote: Set your selves seriously to amend all those faults which they reprove in you

items.text: Honor your husband in your words and behavior; do not speak of his faults behind his back.
items.quote: Honour your Husbands according to their superiority

items.text: Be cheerful and content with your state, bearing poverty or suffering patiently, and do not make your husband's burden heavier.
items.quote: Live in a cheerful contentedness with your condition

items.text: Control your passions and speak and act with meekness and sobriety, so as not to vex your husband.
items.quote: strive to subdue your passions, and to speak and do all in meekness and sobriety

items.text: Be humble and peaceable, not proud or contentious; clothe yourself with humility toward your husband.
items.quote: Take heed of a proud and contentious disposition; and maintain a humble, peaceable temper

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 5 · Special Motives to perswade men to the Holy Governing of their Families. … § 2

items.text: Govern your family as God's officer, keeping them under holy order and constant religious exercises.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 5, §2
items.quote: every Magistrate and Master of a family, doth govern as an Officer of God.

items.text: Do not let your family be ungoverned and ungodly, for it hurries souls to hell; govern well to help save them.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 5, §2
items.quote: an ungoverned ungodly family is a powerful means to the damnation of all the members of it

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 31 … § 36

items.text: Provide for each other's health with wholesome food and guard them from what is harmful.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §31
items.quote: you must be careful to provide for each other (not so much pleasing as) wholsome food, and to keep each other from that which is hurtful to your health

items.text: Tend one another in sickness: spare no cost or pains to restore health and comfort, and do not loathe or shun each other's bodies.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §32
items.quote: you are to be tenderly regardful of each other; and not to be sparing of any cost or pains, by which the health of each other may be restored

items.text: Work together for your daily bread and share the care of your affairs; neither may live in idleness.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §33
items.quote: The care of their affairs doth lye upon them both, and neither of them must cast it off and live in idleness

items.text: Guard each other's good name: conceal private failings and never speak dishonorably of one another to others.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §34
items.quote: You must not divulge, but conceal the dishonourable failings of each other. The reputation of each other must be as dear to you as your own.

items.text: Together train your children and govern the household; each must take a part according to his or her place.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §35
items.quote: They that have a joint interest, and are one flesh, must have a joint part in government: in their places they must divide the care, and help each other.

items.text: Do good to all, especially the household of faith: show hospitality together and do not hinder one another's charity.
items.citation: Christian Directory, II: Christian Oeconomicks, ch. 7, §36
items.quote: help each other in works of charity and hospitality: While they have opportunity to do good to all

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 8 · The special Duties of Husbands to their Wives. · § 8 … § 9

items.text: Lead the household in daily joint prayers to God, standing as its priest, and be holy as you offer up their prayers.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 7
items.quote: The Husband is to be the mouth of the family in their daily conjunct prayers unto God.

items.text: Be the chief provider for the household, and see that your wife and children want nothing fit for them so far as you can procure it.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 8
items.quote: He must be specially careful that wife and children want nothing that is fit for them, so far as he can procure it.

items.text: Bear with your wife's weaknesses and passions, not making a great matter of any frailty against yourself, and so preserve love and peace.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 9
items.quote: The Husband must be strongest in Family-patience; bearing with the weakness and passions of the wife... not make a great matter of any frailty as against himself.

items.text: Treat her with tenderness as the weaker vessel, not in an imperious manner as you would a child or servant, and maintain loving familiarity.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 10
items.quote: not teach or command or reprove a wife, in the same imperious manner as a child or servant.

items.text: Be confident in love, without base suspicions or causeless jealousies.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 10
items.quote: Love be confident, without base suspicions and causless jealousies.

items.text: Do not unjustly conceal secrets that should be common to you both, and do not open to her secrets that would become her snare; keep private family matters from others, and reprove her privately.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 10
items.quote: No unjust and causless concealment of secrets... none of their own matters which should be kept secret be made known to others.

items.text: Be constant in love and duty, not weary of them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 10
items.quote: Be constant, and not weary of his Love or duty.

items.text: Act with prudence in all husbandly duties, not with folly or rashness.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 8, Direct. 10
items.quote: be done in Prudence, and not with folly, rashness and inconsiderateness.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 4 … § 5

items.text: Render due benevolence to your wife, and do not defraud her except by mutual consent for a time of fasting and prayer.
items.quote: Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence

items.text: Render due benevolence to your husband, and do not defraud him except by mutual consent for a time of fasting and prayer.
items.quote: and likewise also the wife unto the husband

items.text: Live together with your wife; do not live apart without great necessity, and do not go overseas or to another land leaving her behind unless it is truly necessary or for public service.
items.quote: live a great part of their lives asunder... is a constant violation of their duties

items.text: Live together with your husband; do not live apart without great necessity.
items.quote: live a great part of their lives asunder... is a constant violation of their duties

items.text: Abhor adultery and all that tends to unchastity or the violation of your marriage covenant; do not let your eye or thought go after a stranger.
items.quote: Abhor not only Adultery it self, but all that tendeth to unchastness and the violation of your Marriage-Covenant.

items.text: Abhor adultery and all that tends to unchastity or the violation of your marriage covenant; do not let your eye or thought go after a stranger.
