items.quote: suffer not your eye or thought to go after a stranger, nor to begin a breach in your Covenant and conjugal fidelity.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 10 · The Duties of Parents for their Children. · § 20 … § 22

items.text: When they are marriageable, look out a suitable match for them in good time, lest they choose blindly.
items.quote: look out such for them as are suitable betimes

items.text: Be diligent in teaching them and speaking to them of what is most necessary, especially while they are young.
items.quote: the Mother who is still present with children when they are young, be very diligent in teaching them, and minding them of good things

items.text: Teach them to read, however poor you are, so they may read the Bible for themselves.
items.quote: By all means let children be taught to read, if you are never so poor

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 6 · More special Motives for a holy and careful Education of Children. … § 2

items.text: Be diligent in the holy education of your children, for nature itself obliges you to their greatest care.
items.quote: Nature it self doth engage you, to the greatest care and diligence for the holy education of your children.

items.text: Do not neglect their souls or be careless of their chief concernments.
items.quote: will you be regardless of their chief concernments? and neglective of their souls?

items.text: Teach them the greatest and most necessary things: to know God, serve him, and be saved.
items.quote: If you teach them not to know God, and how to serve him, and be saved, you teach them nothing, or worse than nothing.

items.text: Bring them up for everlasting happiness, and diligently teach them to escape endless misery.
items.quote: They have an everlasting inheritance of happiness to attain: and it is that which you must bring them up for.

items.text: Do not bring them up in ignorance, carelessness, worldliness, sensuality, and ungodliness, for that is to betray them to the devil and lead them to hell.
items.quote: If you neglect their souls, and breed them in ignorance, worldliness, ungodliness and sin, you betray them to the Devil

items.text: Show your love for them by caring for their everlasting welfare, not by leading them to hell.
items.quote: If you Love them, shew it in those things on which their everlasting welfare doth depend. Do not say you Love them, and yet lead them unto Hell.

items.text: Do not train them up in ignorance of God and in the service of the flesh and world; that is to intend their damnation.
items.quote: you will do by your children if you train them up in ignorance of God, and in the service of the flesh and world

items.text: Resign your children to God, who is their Lord and Owner by creation and redemption, and educate them for him.
items.quote: God is the Lord and Owner of your children, both by the title of Creation and Redemption: Therefore in justice you must resign them to him

items.text: Do not rob God and Christ of your children by giving them to the devil; do not steal them from their absolute Lord and Father.
items.quote: you rob God of his own Creatures, and rob Christ of those for whom he dyed, and this to give them to the Devil steal them from their absolute Lord

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 10 · The Duties of Parents for their Children. … § 4

items.text: Enter them into God's covenant by baptism and dedicate them wholly to him.
items.quote: absolutely resign, and dedicate them to God in Christ in the sacred Covenant, and solemnize this Dedication and Covenant by their Baptism

items.text: Teach them what covenant they are in, its benefits and conditions, and bring them to renew it personally.
items.quote: teach them what a Covenant they are in, and what are the benefits and what the conditions, that their souls may gladly consent to it

items.text: Train them in exact obedience, break their self-will, and do not allow them to be irreverent or contemptuous toward you.
items.quote: Train them up in exact obedience to your selves; and break them of their own wills. To that end, suffer them not to carry themselves unreverently or contemptuously towards you

items.text: Obey your parents exactly, renounce your own will, and show them reverence, not contempt.
items.quote: To be Obedient is to renounce their own wills and be ruled by their Parents or Governours wills

items.text: Govern them as children, not as servants, showing them that you love them and that your commands and corrections are for their good.
items.quote: govern them no as servants, but as Children, making them perceive that you dearly love them, and that all your commands, restraints and corrections are for their good

items.text: Do not be too strange or frightening to them, lest they fear you only and not love you; show tender love, with severity only when they do wrong.
items.quote: tender love, with severity only when they do amiss, and this at a reverend convenient distance, is the only way to do them good

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · § 9 … § 11

items.text: Avoid a childish gaudiness of apparel and costly or troublesome curiosity; such vanity dishonors you and brings shame on your husband.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9, Direct. 9
items.quote: Affect not a childish gawdiness of apparel, nor a vain or costly or troublesom curiosity, in any thing about you.

items.text: Govern your tongue: let your words be few and well considered, so that you may not disgrace your husband by a running tongue.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9, Direct. 10
items.quote: let your words be few, and well considered before you speak them.

items.text: Be willing and diligent in your proper part of the care and labor of the family, especially the secondary provision within doors.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9, Direct. 11
items.quote: Be willing and diligent in your proper part, of the care and labour of the family.

items.text: Nurse your own children, teach them, and watch over them when they are young.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9, Direct. 11
items.quote: nursing your own children, and teaching them, and watching over them when they are young

items.text: Watch over the family at home when your husband is abroad, as your proper work in his stead.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9, Direct. 11
items.quote: watching over the family at home, when your Husbands are abroad

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · Cases about Divorce and Separation.

items.text: Do not put away your wife causelessly; Christ forbids the vicious custom of men's causeless putting away their wives.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9
items.quote: Christ speaketh only of the mans case... to restrain the vicious custome of mens causeless putting away their Wives

items.text: Follow him when he moves, and do not depart from him without warrant; he is the ruler who chooses the habitation.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9
items.quote: it is the man who is to rule and choose the habitation

items.text: If your spouse is an infidel, do not depart or seek divorce; the marriage remains, and you may have conjugal communion.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9
items.quote: it nullifieth not a marriage already made, nor maketh it lawful to depart or divorce: Because they may have meer conjugal Communion still.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 10 · The Duties of Parents for their Children. · § 16 … § 19

items.text: Teach them the preciousness of time and do not let them waste an hour.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 16
items.quote: Teach your children to know the pretiousness of Time, and suffer them not to mispend an hour.

items.text: Train them up in a life of diligence and labour, and do not accustom them to ease and idleness while they are young.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 16
items.quote: Train up your children in a life of diligence and labour, and use them not to ease and idleness when they are young.

items.text: Let necessary correction be neither so seldom as to make them fearless nor so frequent as to discourage them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Let it not be so seldome (if necessary) as to leave them fearless, and so make it uneffectual: and let it not be so frequent as to discourage them.

items.text: Vary correction according to the different temperaments of your children.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Let it be different according to the different tempers of your children.

items.text: Correct more for sins against God than for faults in worldly business.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Let it be more for sin against God (as lying, railing, filthy speaking, prophaneness, &c.) than for faults about your worldly business.

items.text: Do not correct in passion; wait until you are calm so that they perceive reason, not anger.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Correct them not in passion, but stay till they perceive that you are calmed.

items.text: When you correct them, always show tenderness of love and unwillingness to punish, convincing them it is for their good.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Alwayes shew them the tenderness of your Love, and how unwilling you are to correct them.

items.text: Make them read Scripture passages condemning their sin and commanding you to correct them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 17
items.quote: Make them read those Texts of Scripture which condemn their sin, and then those which command you to correct them.

items.text: Let your own example teach them the holiness, heavenliness, and blamelessness of tongue and life that you desire them to learn.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 18
items.quote: Let your own example teach your children that holiness, and heavenliness, and blamelessness of tongue and life, which you desire them to learn and practise.

items.text: Choose a calling and course of life for them that tends most to the saving of their souls and to public usefulness for Church or State, avoiding callings liable to temptations.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 19
items.quote: Choose such a Calling and course of life for your children, as tendeth most to the saving of their souls, and to their publick usefulness for Church or State.

items.text: If you bind them as apprentices or servants, place them if possible with men who fear God, not with those who will harden them in sin.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Ch. 10, § 19
items.quote: If you bind them Apprentices, or Servants, if it be possible place them with men fearing God; and not with such as will harden them in their sin.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 25 … § 30

items.text: Manage differences in religion with holiness, humility, love, and peace, not with carnality, pride, uncharitableness, or contention.
items.quote: If difference in judgement in matters of Religion do fall out between you, be sure that it be managed with Holiness, Humility, Love and Peace

items.text: Do not be blindly indulgent to each other's faults, nor too censorious of each other's state.
items.quote: Be not either blindly indulgent to each others faults, nor yet too censorious of each others state

items.text: If married to an infidel or ungodly person, keep conjugal love due for the relation's sake.
items.quote: If you are married to one that is indeed an infidel, or an ungodly person, yet keep up all the Conjugal Love which is due for the relation sake.

items.text: Join together in frequent and fervent prayer, and pray for each other in secret.
items.quote: Ioyn together in frequent and fervent prayer

items.text: Help each other by an exemplary life; be that yourself which you desire your spouse to be.
items.quote: Help each other by an exemplary life. Be that your selves which you desire your Husband or Wife should be

items.text: Be helpful to each other for health and comfort of body, but not to pamper the flesh.
items.quote: to be helpful to each other for the health and comfort of their Bodies

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 11 · The special Duties of Children towards their Parents. · § 12

items.text: Imitate your parents in all that is good, both when they are living and when they are dead.
items.quote: Imitate your Parents in all that is good, both when they are living, and when they are dead.

items.text: Do not imitate their sin and error; follow them only as they follow Christ.
items.quote: Follow not your Fathers in their sin and error, but follow them where they follow Christ

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 11 · The special Duties of Children towards their Parents. … § 2

items.text: Love your parents dearly and delight to be in their company.
items.quote: Be sure that you dearly love your Parents: Delight to be in their company

items.text: Honor your parents in thought, word, and behavior, and do not speak rudely or contemptuously to them.
items.quote: Honour your Parents both in your Thoughts, and speeches, and behaviour.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · Cases about Divorce and Separation.

items.text: Do not absent yourself from your spouse except for needful and lawful causes, and never out of covetousness; guard against any hurt or neglect that absence may cause.
items.quote: when Covetousness puts them upon it needlesly, and their Wives cannot bear it, or in any case, when the hurt that is like to follow, is greater than the good, it is unlawful.

items.text: Do not put asunder what God has joined; let no prince, pope, or prelate command you to separate without just cause, but if public necessity calls you away for a time, accept it as God's call.
items.quote: what God hath joyned, no man hath power to pu• asunder. Nor can either Prince, Pope or Prelate dispe•se with your Marriage Covenant

items.text: If a prince or office requires you to part from your spouse, rather give up the office than your marriage; obey the law that way.
items.quote: if a Prince say, He that will be a Judge or a Justice shall part with his Wife, it is lawful to leave the Office, and so obey the Law.

items.text: As a minister of the gospel, do not leave your wife without necessity or a clear call from God; but when the church's interest and public good require it, prefer that above family comfort.
items.quote: Those Pastors who have fixed stations, must neither leave flock or family, without necessity, or a clear call from God. But in several Cases a Preacher may be necessitated to go abroad

items.text: Be prepared that your marriage may be interrupted by calls to public duty; do not hinder your spouse from obeying God's call when such necessity arises.
items.quote: Ministers should not rashly venture upon Marriage, nor any woman that is wi•e, venture to marry a Minister, till she is first well prepared for such accidents as may separate them

items.text: If persecution or danger threatens, and your spouse cannot go with you, you may flee to save your life; do not force one another to stay where death is certain.
items.quote: May one leave a Wife to save his life, in case of personal persecution or danger? Answ. Yes, i• she cannot be taken with him: For the means which are for the Helps of Life, do suppose the preservation of Life it self

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 12 · The special Duties of Children and Youth towards God. · § 7 … § 12

items.text: Ask your parents to help your understanding and memory whenever you do not understand or forget what you were taught.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 12, § 10
items.quote: Ask your Parents when you come home, to help your understandings and memories in any thing which you understood not or forgat.

items.text: Choose your trade or calling by the direction of your parents, selecting one that gives the greatest helps for heaven and fewest hindrances.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 12, § 12
items.quote: When you grow up, by the direction of your Parents, choose such a Trade or Calling, as alloweth you the greatest helps for Heaven

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · Cases about Divorce and Separation.

items.text: Do not separate out of mere passion or to gratify vicious tempers; first use all means of reconciliation, and only then part by deliberate free consent.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, II.9 (initial answer on separation)
items.quote: after all other means used in vain) they do it by deliberate free consent

items.text: Do not let impatience make you despair of curing any unsuitableness that is really curable.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, II.9 (initial answer on separation)
items.quote: Nor must impatience make either of them ungroundedly despair of the cure of any unsuitableness which is really curable.

items.text: Lay down the sins that make you unsuited and live together in love and peace; saying you cannot does not free you from the duty.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, II.9 (initial answer on separation)
items.quote: lay down that sin which maketh them unsuitable

items.text: Do not consent to marry another while your spouse lives; marriage is a lifelong covenant, not dissoluble by consent.
items.quote: Marriages pro tempore, dissoluble by consent, are not of Gods institution, but contrary to it.

items.text: If you live apart, remain chaste; do not use your separation to gratify lust or take another spouse.
items.quote: He that will not take heed before, must be patient afterwards, and not make advantage of his own folly, to the fulfilling of his lusts.

items.text: Forgive an adulterous spouse when there is genuine repentance and hope of amendment, as prudence directs.
items.quote: there may be so great repentance, and hope of better effects by forgiving, that it may be a duty to forgive

items.text: When adultery is unrepented and public shame would prevent evil, divorce the adulterer and expose the sin.
items.quote: Sometimes it may be a duty to expose the sin to publick shame, for the prevention of it in others; and also to deliver ones self from a calamity.

heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · Cases about Divorce and Separation.

items.text: Rule your wife in love, not by beating; nothing you do must tend to destroy the love between you.
items.quote: it is unlawful for a man to beat his Wife... because he is by his relation obliged to a Life of Love with her

items.text: Reprove your wife's sin only when it may do good; if reproof makes her worse, bear with her in silence.
items.quote: a Husband may be brought to the same despair with a Wife, and may be disobliged from ordinary reproof

items.text: Do not divorce or cast out your wife even if she is obstinate in sin; keep the marriage bond.
items.quote: the nearness of the Relation forbid him to eject her

items.text: Correct a servant only when it will do good; do not provoke him to violence or greater evil.
items.quote: If my correcting a servant, would make him kill me, or set my house on fire, I may not do it.

items.text: Do not give your wife the means to commit sin when you can avoid it; contribute only when necessity requires.
items.quote: No man may contribute to anothers sin, when he is not naturally or morally necessitated to it, but might forbear it.

items.text: Speak of holy things with the greatest seriousness and reverence, not with levity or rudeness.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 16, § 13
items.quote: Let all your speech of holy things be with the greatest seriousness and reverence

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 8 · The special Duties of Husbands to their Wives. · § 1 … § 7

items.text: Undertake the principal government of your whole household, even of your wife; be fit for it through holiness, wisdom, prudence, justice, and love, and govern yourself well as an example.
items.quote: The Husband must undertake the principal part of the Government of the whole family, even of the Wife her self.

items.text: Unite authority and love so that both are exercised; let your commands be loving, and do not use harshness, cruelty, threats, or blows (except in case of loss of reason).
items.quote: The Husband must so unite Authority and Love, that neither of them may be omitted or concealed, but both be exercised and maintained.

items.text: Support her authority over children and servants; rebuke them if they disobey or mock her (unless her command is unlawful).
items.quote: It is the duty of Husbands to preserve the Authority of their Wives, over the Children and Servants of the family.

items.text: Guard her honor; cover her weaknesses, and do not allow children or servants to mock, despise, or speak rudely to her, but vindicate her from such contempt.
items.quote: you must preserve the Honour as well as the Authority of your Wives.

items.text: Be her spiritual teacher: instruct her from Scripture, direct her duties, help her overcome sin, and confirm her against temptation.
items.quote: The Husband is to excell the Wife in Knowledge, and be her Teacher in the matters that belong to her salvation.

items.text: Be the chief teacher of your household in the faith: instruct, examine, and govern them in godliness, and see that the Lord's Day and worship are observed.
items.quote: The Husband must be the principal Teacher of the family. He must instruct them, and examine them, and rule them about the matters of God.

items.text: Ask your husband to resolve your doubts about faith, and let him explain at home what you did not understand in the congregation.
items.quote: she is to ask his resolution, and he to open to her at home, the things which she understood not in the Congregation.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 18 · CHAP. XVIII. · Tit. 1. Directions for the holy spending of the Lords Day in Families.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · § 12

items.text: Do not dispose of your husband's estate without his knowledge and consent.
items.quote: Dispose not of your Husbands estate without his knowledge and consent.

items.text: Provide necessary food and clothing for your children even if your husband forbids it, rather than let them suffer.
items.quote: if her Husband will not allow her such food and rayment as is necessary to preserve the lives and health of herself and all her Children

items.text: In famine, give from your husband's estate to save the life of one ready to perish, for you are not a stranger to it.
items.quote: Yea and to save the life of another that in famine is ready to perish: For she is not as a stranger to his estate.

items.text: If your husband lives by unlawful gain, admonish him of his sin and danger, endeavor his repentance, and disclaim all consent to his ill-gotten goods.
items.quote: first to admonish her husband of his sin and danger, and endeavour his repentance, in the mean time disclaiming all consent, and reception of the goods.

items.text: Help those whom your husband has injured or robbed to recover their goods, by prudent and just means.
items.quote: help them to their goods whom he hath injured and robbed, (by prudent and just means:)

items.text: If you cannot otherwise prevent your husband from robbing others, reveal his sinful purposes to the magistrate.
items.quote: she seemeth to me to be bound to reveal her husbands sinful purposes to the Magistrate, if she can no other way prevail with him to forbear.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 4 · General Directions for the Holy Government of Families. · § 10 … § 19

items.text: Deal with each member according to his disposition, not all alike.
items.quote: Understand well the different tempers of your inferiors, and deal with them as they are, and as they can bear.

items.text: Differentiate your reproofs according to the fault, being most severe with willfulness and weighty sins.
items.quote: You must much difference between their different faults, and accordingly suit your reprehensions.

items.text: Rule by love so that she sees obedience is for her own good.
items.quote: Be a good Husband to your Wife, and let Love have Dominion in all your Government.

items.text: Rule by love so that they see obedience is for their own good.
items.quote: Be a good Father to your Children, and let Love have Dominion in all your Government.

items.text: Rule by love so that they see obedience is for their own good.
items.quote: Be a good Master to your Servants, and let Love have Dominion in all your Government.

items.text: Command yourself exactly, so that your life does not contradict your reproofs.
items.quote: learn first exactly to command your selves.

items.text: Be holy yourself and subject to God, so that you may govern your family for God.
items.quote: You must be Holy Persons, if you would be Holy Governours of your families: be sure that your own souls be entirely subjected unto God.

items.text: Make the enjoyment of God in glory the ultimate end of your family government.
items.quote: make the enjoyment of God in Glory, to be the ultimate commanding end, both of the affairs and government of your family

items.text: Rebuke sin against God in your children more severely than offenses against yourself.
items.quote: Make not a small matter of any of the sins, especially the Great sins, of your children or servants.

items.text: Rebuke sin against God in your servants more severely than offenses against yourself.
items.quote: Make not a small matter of any of the sins, especially the Great sins, of your children or servants.

items.text: Let spiritual love prevail, making the salvation of their souls your greatest care.
items.quote: Let spiritual Love to your family be predominant, and let your care be greatest for the saving of their souls.

items.text: Keep your family free from idleness and excessive business, so they are not unfitted for holy things.
items.quote: Let your family neither be kept in idleness and flesh-pleasing, nor yet overwhelmed with such a multitude of business

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 19 · Directions for profitable Hearing the Word Preached.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 11 · The special Duties of Children towards their Parents. · § 5 … § 11

items.text: Submit to any labor your parents appoint you; do not murmur that it is low, hard, or tedious, nor prefer idleness and play.
items.quote: Humble your selves and submit to any labour that your Parents shall appoint you to.

items.text: Be willing and thankful to be instructed by your parents, especially about the fear of God and the matters of your salvation.
items.quote: Be willing and thankful to be instructed by your Parents, or any of your Teachers, but especially about the fear of God, and the matters of your salvation.

items.text: Patiently submit to the correction your parents lay upon you; accept it as God's appointed means for your good, and do not be angry with them.
items.quote: Patiently submit to the correction which your Parents lay upon you.

items.text: Do not choose your own companions; use the company your parents appoint you, because bad company is the first undoing of a child.
items.quote: Choose not your own company, but use such company as by your Parents is appointed you.

items.text: Do not choose your own calling or trade without the choice or consent of your parents; bring your will to theirs, unless they choose something unlawful.
items.quote: Choose not your own Calling or Trade of life without the choice or consent of your Parents.

items.text: Do not marry without your parents' consent; if possible, let their choice of the person come before your own, because unexperienced youth chooses by fancy and passion.
items.quote: Marry not without your Parents consent: Nay, if it may be, let their choice determine first of the person, and not your own.

items.text: While you can live in chastity, remain unmarried if your parents will not consent to a suitable match; do not pretend a necessity from your own affections.
items.quote: you must remain unmarried, while by the use of right means you can live in chastity, till your Parents are in a better mind.

items.text: If your parents are in want, relieve them according to your ability; wholly maintain them if there is need, and let them live as your superiors, not as inferiors.
items.quote: If your Parents be in want, it is your duty to relieve them according to your ability: yea, and wholly to maintain them if there be need.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 11 · The special Duties of Children towards their Parents. · § 3 … § 4

items.text: Obey your parents in all things that God does not forbid, readily, without murmuring, disputing, or setting your own will against theirs.
items.quote: Obey your Parents in all things (which God forbiddeth not.) ... readily obey their commands without unwillingness, murmuring or disputing.

items.text: Hearken to your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching; do not despise your mother when she is old.
items.quote: Hearken unto thy Father that begat thee, and despise not thy Mother when she is old... hear the instruction of thy Father, and forsake not the law of thy Mother.

items.text: Even after you are married and have your own estate, still obey your parents in all things for which they are appointed to help and guide you.
items.quote: if they command you your duty to God or them, you are still obliged to obey them

items.text: Be content with your parents' provision and disposal of you; do not murmur or complain about food, clothing, or restrictions.
items.quote: Be contented with your Parents provision for you, and disposal of you: Do not rebelliously murmur against them, and complain of their usage of you;

items.text: Do not take anything from your parents against their will, and do not be eager to have your own way or be at your own disposal.
items.quote: much less take any thing against their wills ... desire not to be at your own dispose

items.text: Be thankful for what your parents give you, remembering that you do not deserve it but receive it freely.
items.quote: Be thankful for what you have, and remember that you deserve it not, but have it freely

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 21 · Directions for Reading other Books. · § 11 … § 13

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 10 · The Duties of Parents for their Children. · § 9 … § 12

items.text: Teach them to hate flesh-pleasing and to value the pleasures of wisdom and doing good; speak against gluttony, drunkenness, and excessive sport, and make them learn and repeat the appointed Scriptures.
items.quote: Speak often to them of the bruitish baseness and sinfulness of flesh-pleasing sensuality, and of the greater excellency of the Pleasures of the mind

items.text: Keep a strict guard on their appetites, allowing them food in quantity and quality according to reason, not their craving, and use them to temperance from infancy.
items.quote: Keep a strict guard upon their appetites... in both the quantity and quality of their food.

items.text: Allow them sports and recreations as needed for health and cheerfulness, but limit them so they do not steal their minds from better things or tempt them to gaming or covetousness.
items.quote: let them be such and so much as may be needful to their health and cheerfulness: but not so much as may carry away their minds from better things

items.text: Commend humility and plainness to them, speak disgracefully of pride and fineness, teach them Scripture against pride, and abhor boasting while giving due praise for what is well.
items.quote: commend humility and plainness to them, and speak disgracefully of Pride and fineness, to breed an aversness to it in their minds

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 13 · The Duties of Servants to their Masters. · § 5 … § 12

items.text: Be true and faithful in all that is committed to your trust: dispose not of any thing of your master's without his consent, and if you have defrauded him, make restitution.
items.quote: Be true and faithful in all that is committed to your trust: Dispose not of any thing that is your Masters without his consent.

items.text: Honor your masters with respect and reverence; give no saucy or contemptuous language, and do not despise them even if they are your brothers in Christ.
items.quote: Honour your Masters, and behave your selves towards them with that respect and reverence as your place requireth.

items.text: Do your work heartily and willingly, not grudgingly or murmuring, as to the Lord.
items.quote: Go not unwillingly or murmuringly about your business, but take it as your delight. Do service heartily, and with good will as to the Lord.

items.text: Obey your masters in all things that God does not forbid and that their place enables them to command, and set not your own opinions against their commands.
items.quote: Obey your Masters in all things (which God forbiddeth not, and which their place enableth them to command you) and set not your own conceits and wills against their commands.

items.text: Reveal not the secrets of your masters or of the family; do not talk to others of what is said or done at home.
items.quote: Reveal not any of the secrets of your Masters, or of the family.

items.text: Do not grudge at the meanness of the family's provisions; if you have necessary wholesome food, murmur not for more delicious fare.
items.quote: Grudge not at the meanness of the provisions of the family. If you have your daily bread... murmur not for want of more delicious fare.

items.text: Pray daily for a blessing on your labors and on the family, both privately and with the rest.
items.quote: Pray daily for a blessing on your labours and on the family, both privately and with the rest.

items.text: Willingly submit to your master's teaching and government about the right worship of God and for the good of your soul; be glad of his instructions and do not murmur at them.
items.quote: Willingly submit to the teaching and government of your masters about the right worshipping of God, and for the good of your own souls.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 13 · The Duties of Servants to their Masters. … § 4

items.text: Do not murmur at your labor or low condition; be thankful for your lot.
items.quote: murmur not at your labour, or your low condition; but know your mercies, and be thankful for them

items.text: Serve him heartily as unto the Lord, not with eye-service or as men-pleasers.
items.quote: do it heartily as to the Lord, and not unto men

items.text: Be faithful and conscientious in all your labor: do not neglect, idle, or deceive him of time or service.
items.quote: Be consc•ionable and faithful in performing all the labour and duty of a servant. Neglect not such business as you are to do: nor do it not lazily, and deceitfully, and by the halves.

items.text: Be more careful about your duty to him than about his duty to you.
items.quote: Be more careful about your duty to your Masters, than about their duty or carriage to you.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 12 · The special Duties of Children and Youth towards God. … § 6

items.text: Willingly own and perform the covenant your parents made on your behalf with God; do not grudge their authority in it.
items.citation: Baxter, A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 12, § 6
items.quote: openly with thankfulness to own the Covenant in which you are engaged

items.text: Do not let excessive love of play or food destroy your love for your parents or your duty to them.
items.citation: Baxter, A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 12, § 6
items.quote: destroyeth the love of their Books, and their duty, and their Parents themselves

items.text: Submit your will to your parents; be content with what they allow, and do not be importunate or discontent when they deny you.
items.citation: Baxter, A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 12, § 6
items.quote: Subdue your own wills and desires to the will of God and your superiours

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · § 12

items.text: Obey him when he forbids hearing unnecessary sermons, when no greater duty calls you away.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: in this case, the Command of a Husband, with the inconveniences that will follow disobeying him, may make it a duty to forbear.

items.text: In all differences of judgment, exercise self-suspicion, modesty, and submission, acknowledging the weakness of your sex and your subjection to him.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: the Wife must exercise such self-suspicion, and modesty, and submission, as may signifie her due sense, both of the weakness of her Sex, and of her subjection to her Husband.

items.text: In things indifferent, obey him in practice, unless a higher authority forbids.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: In things indifferent she must in practice obey her Husband; unless when superiour powers do forbid it, and that in cases where their authority is greater.

items.text: She may modestly give her reasons of dissent, but must not turn disagreement into quarrel, disaffection, or pretense against her conjugal duties.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: She may modestly give her reasons of dissent. She must not turn it to an unpeaceable quarrel, or matter of disaffection, or pretend any differences against her Conjugal duties.

items.text: In dark and difficult cases, do not be peremptory or importunate; if you have more knowledge than he, keep it to yourself in quietness and silence.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: In dark and difficult cases she should not be peremptory, and self-conceited, nor importunate; but if she have faith ... have it to her self, in quietness and silence.

items.text: If he is in dangerous error, wisely but unweariedly seek his reformation, by yourself or others.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: If a Husband be in dangerous error, she must wisely, but unweariedly seek his reformation, by her self or others.

items.text: If speaking against his vice makes him worse, do not cease to seek his good: use gentle persuasion, indirect means, and continue conjugal affection and duty.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 9, § 12
items.quote: she is to continue all Conjugal affection and duty, and a convincing, winning course of life, which may prove the most effectual reproof.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 7 · The mutual Duties of Husbands and Wives towards each other. · § 37 … § 38

items.text: Be helpers and comforters of each other in order to a safe and happy death.
items.quote: It is a great part of the duty of Husbands and Wives, to be helpers and comforters of each other in order to a safe and happy death.

items.text: In time of health, often and seriously remember each other of the time when death will make the separation, and live together expecting the parting hour.
items.quote: you must often and seriously remember each other of the time when death will make the separation; and live together in your daily converse, as those that are still expecting the parting hour.

items.text: Help to awaken each other's souls to make ready all graces necessary and live in constant preparation for your change.
items.quote: Help to awaken each others souls, to make ready all those graces which then will prove necessary, and to live in a constant preparation for your change.

items.text: Reprove all in one another that will be unsavoury and ungrateful to your review at death.
items.quote: Reprove all that in one another, which will be unsavoury and ungrateful to your review at death.

items.text: If you see each other dull and slow in preparations or living in vanity, worldliness, or sloth, stir up one another to do without delay what death requires.
items.quote: If you see each other dull and slow in your preparations... stir up one another to do all that without delay which the approach of such a day requireth.

items.text: When death is at hand, give wise, faithful, diligent help; show compassion and speak serious counsel and comfort to the departing soul.
items.quote: when nature faileth... a languishing body, and a doubting, fearful, troubled mind, do call for your compassion and help... speak a serious word of counsel or comfort to you at a dying hour.

items.text: Live together as heirs of heaven, help and encourage each other's souls, and joyfully part at death expecting to meet in life eternal.
items.quote: they that live together as the heirs of Heaven... may help and encourage the souls of one another, and joyfully part at death, as expecting quickly to meet again in life eternal.

items.text: Do all your duties to each other in entire love, making each other's case as your own.
items.quote: it should be all done in such entire Love, as maketh the case of one another to you as your own.

items.text: Do all in patience and mutual forbearance.
items.quote: all must be done in Patience and mutual forbearance.

items.text: Deal with each other in familiarity, not with strangeness, distance, sowerness, or affected complement.
items.quote: in familiarity, and not with strangeness, distance, sowerness, nor affected complement.

items.text: Trust each other's fidelity; do not give way to suspicion, jealousy, or distrust.
items.quote: in confidence of each others fidelity, and not in suspicion, jealousie, and distrust.

items.text: Remain constant in your duties to one another until death.
items.quote: in constancy that you cease not your duties for one another until death.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 10 · The Duties of Parents for their Children. · § 5 … § 8

items.text: Possess their hearts with the fear of God and reverence for holy Scripture; when you command or forbid, show them plain and urgent texts of Scripture and have them learn and repeat them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 5
items.quote: whatsoever duty you command them, or whatever sin you forbid them, shew them some plain and urgent Texts of Scripture

items.text: Speak always of God, Jesus Christ, Scripture, the life to come, and holy duties with gravity, seriousness, and reverence, so that your children receive a general reverence for holy things.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 6
items.quote: speak alwaies with gravity, seriousness and reverence, as of the most great and dreadful and most sacred things

items.text: Speak before your children with great honor and praise of holy ministers and people, and with dispraise and loathing of every sin and ungodly men.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 7
items.quote: Speak alwayes before them with great honour and praise of Holy Ministers and people, and with dispraise and loathing of every sin and of ungodly men.

items.text: Make holiness appear to your children as the most necessary, honorable, gainful, pleasant, delightful, and amiable state of life, and keep them from thinking it needless, dishonorable, hurtful, or uncomfortable.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 8
items.quote: make Holiness appear to them the most Necessary, Honourable, gainful, pleasant delightful amiable state of life

items.text: In restraining them from sin, go to the highest step at first; do not allow even the least degree of sin.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 8
items.quote: in restraining them from sin, you must go to the highest step at first, and not think to draw them from it by allowing them the least degree

items.text: Carry them on by degrees in the practice of religious duties; do not put more on them than they can bear, neither in quality nor quantity, lest they grow weary of religion.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 10, § 8
items.quote: you must carry them on by degrees, and put them at first upon no more than they can bear

heading: Chapter 9 · The special Duties of Wives to Husbands. · Cases about Divorce and Separation.

items.text: Follow your husband when his removal is like to do good or when you are a settled Christian not endangered.
items.quote: if she be a confirmed wellsetled Christian... it seemeth to me the safest way to follow her Husband.

items.text: Do not use your authority to lead your wife where she would lose public worship or be exposed to spiritual hazard.
items.quote: nor hath God given her Husband any power to do her so much wrong

items.text: Follow your husband even to the loss of your estate if it is for greater spiritual gain.
items.quote: If it be for greater spiritual gain (as in his case) she is bound to follow him.

items.text: Remain under your husband's government; you cannot contract yourself out of it.
items.quote: she can by no Contract, except her self from his true Government.

items.text: If you cannot live continently in his absence, endure the greatest sufferings rather than risk incontinency by staying apart.
items.quote: whether she can live continently in his absence: otherwise the greatest sufferings must be endured, to avoid incontinency.

items.text: Do not take your spouse's life; you have no power to deprive one another of life.
items.quote: they shall have no power to deprive one another of life

items.text: Love your spouse and do not separate because of fixed hatred; wait, pray, and strive by love and goodness to recover love.
items.quote: you must do your duty, and wait, and pray, and strive by Love and Goodness to recover Love, and then stay

items.text: Do not forbid your wife to read the Scriptures or to attend public or private worship.
items.quote: will not suffer her to read the Scriptures, nor go to Gods Worship publick or private

items.text: Do not scold at your husband when he is praying or instructing the family; do not make it impossible for him to serve God with freedom and peace.
items.quote: a Wife that will scold at him when he is praying or instructing his family, and make it impossible to him to serve God with freedome

items.text: Secure yourself and your children from being ruined by your husband's willful folly.

items.text: Treat a slave as a brother, not merely as a bondman, exercising brotherly love in all dealings.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: the same man is a servant and a brother, and therefore must at once be used as both.

items.text: Do not hinder his salvation or deprive him of the means of grace; but seek his sanctification and comfort.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: No man may be put to such a slavery ... as shall injure Gods interest and service, or the mans salvation.

items.text: Pay him his due wages and do not keep back his hire by fraud.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: the hire of the labourers ... kept back by fraud, cryeth

items.text: Do not buy or use a man as a slave when it would bring him into misery or deprive him of the comforts that nature gives to man as man; exercise charity.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: yet is it not lawful for any other so to take advantage by his necessity, as to bring him into a condition, that shall make him miserable, or in which we shall not exercise so much love, as may tend to his sanctification, comfort and salvation.

items.text: Show greater love and brotherly tenderness to slaves who are real Christians.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: good and real Christians must be used with more Love and brotherly tenderness than others.

items.text: Invite slaves to Christianity by offering them greater privileges when they turn Christian.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: they should know that if they will turn Christians they shall have more priviledges and emoluments than the enemies of truth and piety shall have.

items.text: Do not use slaves as beasts for mere commodity, nor betray, destroy, or neglect their souls.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 14, Tit. 2 Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves
items.quote: they that buy them and use them as beasts, for their meer commodity, and betray or destroy or neglect their souls, are fitter to be called incarnate Devils than Christians.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 14 · The Duties of Masters towards their Servants. · Tit. 2. Directions to those Masters in foraign Plantations who have Negro's and other Slaves; being a solution of several Cases about them.

items.text: Treat your slaves as fellow reasonable creatures, not as brutes; allow them due time and seasons for the duties God has made theirs, and do not hinder their salvation.
items.quote: they have immortal souls, and are equally capable of salvation with your selves... allow them due time and seasons for that which God hath made their duty.

items.text: Remember God is their absolute Owner; serve His interest in them first, above your own profit or convenience.
items.quote: Remember that God is their absolute Owner... Gods interest in them, and by them must be served first.

items.text: Command them nothing that God forbids, and do not expect your commands to be preferred before God's.
items.quote: you have no power to command them to omit any duty which God commandeth them, nor to commit any sin which God forbiddeth them.

items.text: Use even the meanest of them with the love and respect due to those whom God loves as His own.
items.quote: God is their Reconciled tender Father... you must use the meanest of them no otherwise, than beseemeth the Beloved of God to be used.

items.text: So use your slaves as to preserve Christ's right and interest in them, for He has redeemed them.
items.quote: they are the Redeemed ones of Christ... So use them, as to preserve Christs right and interest in them.

items.text: As guardians of their souls, bring your slaves to the knowledge and faith of Christ and to obedience to God's commands.
items.quote: you are Christs Trustees, or the Guardians of their souls... bring them to the Knowledge and faith of Christ, and to the just obedience of Gods commands.

items.text: Do not keep your slaves from hearing God's word or from becoming Christians for fear of losing their service or profit.
items.quote: keep their Negro's and slaves from hearing Gods word, and from becoming Christians

items.text: Do not buy or use them merely as you would horses, for your own commodity; treat them as men with souls.
items.quote: Do you not buy them and use them meerly to the same end, as you do your horses? to labour for your commodity!

items.text: Labor for a full and lively heart, so that your holy conference with fellow servants may be serious and edifying to them.
items.quote: Labour most for a full and lively heart which hath the feeling of those things which your tongues should speak of

items.text: Even when your heart is cold, force your tongue to speak of holy things to your fellow servants, and do not remain silent until you feel moved.
items.quote: force your tongues to do their duty, if they will not do them freely without constraint

items.text: Study to understand the things of God, so that you may speak discreetly and profitably to your fellow servants; if you lack knowledge, ask for instruction.
items.quote: Labour to be furnished with understanding in the matters of God

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 15 · The Duties of Children and Fellow-servants to one another. … § 7

items.text: Love one another unfeignedly as yourselves; avoid all contention, envy, and seeking your own honor, and in honor prefer one another.
items.quote: Love one another unfeignedly as your selves: Avoid all contention and falling out... Take heed of the Spirit of envy... Give place to others, and in honour prefer others.

items.text: Refrain from provoking words; put away all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and evil speaking; be kind, tenderhearted, and forgiving one another.
items.quote: Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice: and be ye kind one to another, tender hearted, forgiving one another.

items.text: Help one another with love and willingness in your labors, and do not grudge that another works less than you, but be as ready to help as you would want help yourself.
items.quote: Help one another with love and willingness in your labours: and do not grudge at one another... be as ready to help another, as you would be helpt your selves.

items.text: Do not tempt one another to sin, especially through immodest familiarity between men and women; keep from wanton dalliance and unchaste words.
items.quote: Take heed that you prove not Tempters to draw each other to sin... lest immodest familiarity draw those of different sexes into a snare.

items.text: Watch over one another; agree to tell one another of your faults in love, and receive reproof thankfully without anger, excuse, or retaliation.
items.quote: Watch over one another for mutual preservation against the sin... Agree to tell each other of your faults, not proudly or passionately, but in love: and resolve to take it thankfully from each other.

items.text: When together, let your talk be edifying; speak of God's Word and heavenly things, and put away all corrupt, foolish, or jesting speech.
items.quote: let your discourse be such as tendeth to edification... provoke one another to the Love of God, and holy duty... Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth.

items.text: Patiently bear with one another's personal failings and forgive private offenses, but do not conceal faults that would harm your master or others.
items.quote: Patiently bear with the failings of one another... But conceal not those faults which will be cherished by concealment, or whose concealment tendeth to the wrong of your Master, or any other.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 14 · The Duties of Masters towards their Servants. … § 10

items.text: Rule them not tyrannically but in tenderness and love, and command nothing against the laws of God or the good of their souls.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 1
items.quote: rule them not tyrannically but in tenderness and love: and command them nothing that is against the Laws of God, or the good of their souls.

items.text: Use not wrath or unmanlike fury; rebuke only in season, with prudence and sobriety, when it is likely to do good.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 1
items.quote: Find fault in season, with prudence and sobriety, when your passions are down

items.text: Provide them work that they are fit for, not so much as to harm their health or hinder their salvation, nor so little as to cherish idleness.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 2
items.quote: Provide them work convenient for them, and such as they are fit for; Not such or so much as to wrong them in their health, or hinder them from the necessary means of their salvation

items.text: Do not overwork them so that they have no time to pray before work or are too tired for prayer, instruction, or the Lord's Day worship.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 2
items.quote: let not their labours be so great, as shall allow them no time to pray before they go about it

items.text: Give them wholesome food and lodging and the wages their service deserves or that you promised.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 3
items.quote: Provide them such wholsome food and lodging, and such wages as their service doth deserve

items.text: Do not be so familiar with them that they despise you, nor so distant that you lose opportunity to speak to them for their spiritual good or appear too proud.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 4
items.quote: nor yet so strange and distant as may deprive you of opportunity of speaking to them for their spiritual good

items.text: Keep them to the constant worship of God, especially on the Lord's Day in public and private.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 5
items.quote: keep them to the constant worshipping of God, especially on the Lords day, in publick and private

items.text: Teach them the things that concern their salvation and pray for them daily.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 5
items.quote: teach them the things that concern their salvation ... And pray for them daily

items.text: Watch over them that they do not offend God, and do not tolerate ungodliness or gross sin in your family.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 6
items.quote: Watch over them that they offend not God: Bear not with ungodliness or gross sin

items.text: Keep them from evil company and from being temptations to one another as far as you can.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 7
items.quote: Keep your servants from evil company, and from being temptations to each other

items.text: Go before them as examples of holiness, wisdom, and all virtues you would teach them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 8
items.quote: Go before them as examples of holiness and wisdom

items.text: Patiently bear with their tolerable frailties and infirmities which they commit against their wills.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks, Chapter 14, Direct. 9
items.quote: Patiently bear with those tolerable frailties ... against their wills

items.text: Warn them against the love of the world and covetousness; tell them heaven excels earthly riches and the poor believer is happier.
items.quote: Speak to them disgracefully of the Gallantry and pomp and Riches of the world, and of the sin of selfishness and covetousness: and diligently watch against it

items.text: Do not entice them to worldliness by giving money, allowing gambling, promising wealth, or praising the rich.
items.quote: Do not as the wicked, that entice their Children to worldliness and covetousness, by giving them money, and letting them game and play for money

items.text: Teach them to love their brethren as themselves and to give part of what they have; praise generosity and blame greed.
items.quote: Teach them how good it is to love their brethren as themselves, and to give them part of what they have; and praise them for it

items.text: Watch carefully over their speech; do not pass over lying, railing, ribald talk, or taking God's name in vain, but teach them the odiousness of these sins.
items.quote: Narrowly watch their tongues, especially against Lying, railing, ribbald talk, and taking the name of God in vain; and never pass it by

items.text: Keep them as much as possible from ill company, especially ungodly playfellows.
items.quote: Keep them as much as may be from ill company, especially of ungodly play-fellows

items.text: If able, educate them at home or in private well-ordered schools rather than common schools.
items.quote: let those that are able, either educate their Children most at home, or in private and well ordered Schools

items.text: If they must attend common schools, be extra watchful, charge them to associate with the best, and speak disgracefully of ungodly children.
items.quote: must be the more exceeding watchful over them, and charge them to associate with the best; and speak to them of the odiousness of these practises

items.text: Do not send a young, unsettled child to travel among Papists and profane people merely to see the world.
items.quote: To send young, raw, unsettled persons, among Papists, and prophane licentious people... only to see the Countreys and fashions of the World

items.text: Govern your wife as a wife, not as a servant; do not be sinfully indulgent or remiss like Eli.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9
items.quote: though a Wife must be Governed as a Wife, and a Child as a Child, yet all must be governed as well as servants.

items.text: Do everything you lawfully can to cure and prevent her sin; do not forbear hindering it through indifference, sloth, or fear of fleshly suffering, but only if truly unable.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9
items.quote: leave nothing undone that you can lawfully do, for the cure and prevention of others sins

items.text: Care for her bodily life, health, and peace as a duty; you may give money or materials she is likely to misuse because that duty outweighs preventing a particular sin.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9
items.quote: your own duties to mens bodies (as to save mens lives or health or peace) is to be numbred with spiritual things

items.text: Provide for your family and relieve the poor as God's steward; give strict account of your talents, and do not allow great wastefulness of the estate.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9
items.quote: A mans duty to relieve the poor and provide for his family is so great, that it must be a great reason indeed

items.text: If she is incurably wasteful or mad, restrain her as one restrains the mad, rather than let God's goods be wasted by the Devil.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 9
items.quote: it were better deal with such a Woman as a Bedlam, and if she will be mad, to use her as the mad are used

items.text: Care for his soul: give him time to learn God's word, to pray, and to rest and worship on the Lord's Day; instruct, exhort, and keep him from sin.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, ¶1
items.quote: He must have time to learn the word of God, and time to pray, and he must rest on the Lords day... He must be instructed and exhorted and kept from sin.

items.text: Do not force him to commit any sin against God.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, ¶1
items.quote: He may not be forced to commit any sin against God.

items.text: Do not deny him the comforts of life needful for cheerful serving of God, his daily bread.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, ¶1
items.quote: denyed such comforts of this life, as are needful to his cheerful serving of God... our Daily bread.

items.text: Even in punishing a criminal slave, do not force him to sin or deny necessary helps to salvation; keep punishment within true justice.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, ¶2
items.quote: The most criminal slave may not be forced to sin, nor denyed necessary helps to his salvation... not done more rigorously than true Justice.

items.text: If you have bought a slave who was stolen or sold without right, set him free at once; do not sell him or send him back to the seller.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Quest.
items.quote: undoubtedly they are presently bound to deliver them: Because by right the man is his own.

items.text: Prefer God's interest and their spiritual and eternal happiness; teach them the way to heaven and do all for their souls as for other servants; if they are infidels, win them by your holy example.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Direct. 3
items.quote: prefer Gods interest, and their spiritual and everlasting happiness... Teach them the way to Heaven... use them so as tendeth to win them to Christ.

items.text: Pity them in their hard condition; labor to abate their burden and sweeten their lives, loving them as yourself and doing to them as you would be done by.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Direct. 4
items.quote: let your charity pity them, and labour to abate their burden, and sweeten their lives... love as your selves.

items.text: Require no more of an innocent slave than you would of an ordinary servant who was at your will.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Direct. 5
items.quote: you may require no more of an innocent slave, than you would or might do of an ordinary servant.

items.text: If they are infidels, be neither too hasty nor too slow in baptizing them; hasten their learning and desires, and when they are fit, have them baptized.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Direct. 6
items.quote: be too hasty in baptizing them... Nor yet so slow... hasten them to Learn... when you see them fit... put them on to be baptized.

items.text: Make winning them to Christ and saving their souls your chief end in buying and using slaves; value their salvation above their service, and treat them as fellow redeemed.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 14, Tit. 2, Direct. 7
items.quote: Make it your chief end in buying and using slaves, to win them to Christ and save their souls... let their salvation be far more valued... live with them in the liberty of the Saints.

items.text: Suffer patiently what your husband inflicts on you.
items.quote: The Woman must ... suffer patiently what is inflicted on her: Martyrdome may be as comfortably suffered from a Husband, as from a Prince.

items.text: Cohabit with your spouse who has an innocent disease, and tenderly cherish and comfort him or her, even at some risk to your own life.
items.quote: the other must co-habite, and tenderly cherish and comfort the diseased; yea, so as somewhat to hazard their own lives

items.text: If separated by mutual consent or for self-preservation, do not marry another; wait for possible reconciliation.
items.quote: They that part by consent, to avoid mutual hurt, may not marry again... the innocent party must wait to see whether there be any hope of a return.

items.text: Endure a short desertion by your spouse in hope of reconciliation.
items.quote: A short desertion must be endured in hope

items.text: Restrain your wife from beating you or doing intolerable things, using lawful means such as the magistrate, denying privileges, or necessary physical restraint.
items.quote: the man hath more means to restrain his Wife from beating him, or doing such intollerable things... as belongeth to a Conjugal Ruler.

items.text: Do not tolerate known sin in your household if it is in your power to correct it.
items.quote: not Lawful... to allow of sin, nor to tollerate it, or leave it uncured, when it is truly in our power to cure it.

items.text: Do not correct a child or servant, or turn him away, if your husband forbids it.
items.quote: The Wife may not correct a Child or Servant, or turn him away, when the Husband forbiddeth it.

items.text: See that your servants dispatch all their business before the Lord's Day.
items.quote: Dispatch all your business, that you may not have it then to hinder and disturb you: And see that your Servants do the same.

items.text: Cause your servants to remember the doctrine taught last Lord's Day.
items.quote: if you have servants, cause them to remember it

items.text: Go to bed at a seasonable hour so that your servants are not forced to lie long or be sleepy on the Lord's Day.
items.quote: Go seasonably to bed that you and your servants may not be constrained to lye long the next morning, or be sleepy on the Lords day.

items.text: Lead family worship seriously and reverently, suited to the nature of the day.
items.quote: Let Family-worship come next, and not be slubbered over sleightly, but be serious and reverent

items.text: Call your family together after dinner, sing a psalm of praise, and help them remember what was publicly taught.
items.quote: After dinner call your families together, and sing a Psalm of Praise, and ... cause them to remember what was publickly taught them.

items.text: Call your family together in the evening for prayer, praise, and repetition of the sermon.
items.quote: When you come home call your families together, and first crave Gods assistance and acceptance: and then sing a Psalm of Praise: and then repeat the Sermon

items.text: Allow your servants time for private prayer and meditation, burdening them with no more work than necessary.
items.quote: let your Servants, have no more to hinder them from the same priviledge, than what is of Necessity.

heading: Chapter 21 · Directions for Reading other Books. … § 10

items.text: Keep out of the house all idle, false, or seducing books that corrupt the mind.
items.quote: keep the Devils Books out of your hands and house: I mean Cards, and idle Tales, and Play-books, and Romances or Love-books

items.text: Read to your family at a seasonable and quiet time when they can attend without distraction.
items.quote: let it be seasonably and gravely, when silence and attendance encourage you to expect success; and not when children are crying or talking

items.text: Choose books suited to the spiritual condition of those who hear.
items.quote: Choose such Books as are most suitable to your state or to those you read to.

items.text: For a common family, begin with books that inform the judgment on fundamentals and awaken the affections.
items.quote: To a common family begin with those Books, which at once inform the judgement about the Fundamentals, and awaken the affections

items.text: After those, read books suited to young Christians for growth in grace and mortifying of sin.
items.quote: Next these read over those Books which are more suited to the state of young Christians for their growth in grace

items.text: Teach the family a short catechism, then a larger one, and then a body of divinity, and see that the catechism is kept in memory.
items.quote: read first and learn some short Catechism, and then some larger... and next some Body of Divinity... and let the Catechisme be kept in memory

items.text: Read to the family larger expositions of the Creed, Lord's Prayer, and Ten Commandments for a fuller understanding.
items.quote: read the larger Expositions of the Creed, Lords Prayer and Ten Commandments... that your understanding may be more full

items.text: Read much to the family books that direct daily communion with God and ordering of all conversation.
items.quote: Read much those Books which direct you in a course of daily communion with God, and ordering all your conversations

items.text: Read to the family books for peace, comfort, and increase of love to God.
items.quote: For Peace, and Comfort, and encrease of the Love of God read Mr. Symmonds Deserted Soul, &c.

items.text: Provide and use annotated Bibles or commentaries for understanding the text of Scripture.
items.quote: For the understanding of the Text of Scripture, keep at hand, either Deodates or the Assembly of Divines, or the Dutch Annotations

items.text: Lead the family in prayer yourself unless you are utterly unfit; then delegate it to another.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 1
items.quote: Let it be done rather by the Master of the family himself than any other, if he be competently able

items.text: Adapt family prayer to the needs and condition of those who join in it.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 2
items.quote: Let prayer be suited to the case of those that joyn in it

items.text: Keep family prayer long enough to warm hearts but not so long as to burden them.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 3
items.quote: Let it neither be so short as to end before their hearts can be warm... nor yet so tedious as to make it an ungrateful burden

items.text: Pray with such earnestness that you keep the family awake and attentive.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 4
items.quote: keep waken your own heart, that you may keep the rest awake, and force them to attention

items.text: Schedule family prayer at a time when the family is least distracted or tired.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 5
items.quote: Pray at such hours as the family may be least distracted, sleepy, tired

items.text: Include Scripture reading and psalm singing as aids to family prayer.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 6
items.quote: Let other duties concurr as oft as may be to assist in prayer: as Reading and Singing Psalms.

items.text: Conduct family prayer with genuine reverence for God, not mere outward show.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 7
items.quote: Do all with the greatest reverence of God that possibly you can: Not seeming Reverence, but Real

items.text: Choose fitting words in prayer for the sake of the hearers; if unable to do so, use a well-composed form.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 8
items.quote: The more the bearers are concerned in it, the more regard you must have to the fitness of your expressions

items.text: Prefer public church prayer over family prayer, and do not schedule family prayer at the same time.
items.citation: Christian Directory, Part II, Chapter 23, Tit. 3, §. 9
items.quote: Let not family Prayer be used at the time of publick prayer in the Church, nor preferred before it

items.text: Settle your estate before your death, providing for your children; but if your children are wicked, do not leave them more than their daily bread; give to charitable uses instead.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Chap. 30, Tit. 3, Direct. 16
items.quote: especially they that have no Children, or such wicked Children, as are like to do hurt with all that is given them above their daily bread.
