heading: Chapter 31 · Directions to the Friends of the Sick that are about them. · § 1 … § 6

items.text: Seek the best medical aid from able physicians for your sick kinsman.
items.quote: Use the best means for the recovery of the sick, which the ablest Physicions shall advise you to, as far as you are able.

items.text: Urge your sick kinsman to make his will and settle his estate to prevent contention.
items.quote: Mind your friends betimes to make their Wills, and prudently by good advice to settle their estates

items.text: Provide the sick with spiritual counsel from a faithful minister and prayerful Christians, and keep away distracting company.
items.quote: Procure some able faithful Minister to be with them to counsel them about the state of their souls: And get some holy able Christians to be much about them

items.text: Endure the sick person's impatience with love, tenderness, compassion, and patience.
items.quote: Bear with their impatience, and grudge not at any trouble that they put you to... Be not weary of your friends in sickness; but loving, and tender, and compassionate, and patient.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 29 · Directions for the Aged (and weak). · § 13 … § 15

items.text: Honor God by patient suffering, and be an example of faith, patience, and heavenly-mindedness to all about you.
items.quote: be examples of faith and patience and heavenly-mindedness, and confidence and joy in God, to all about them.

items.text: Let your joyful expectation of death and earnest desire to be with Christ show others that heaven is real and a holy life is best.
items.quote: Live in the joyful expectations of your change, as becometh one that is so near to Heaven, and looketh to live with Christ for ever.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 31 · Directions to the Friends of the Sick that are about them. · § 7 … § 12

items.text: Do not flatter the sick with vain hopes of life when they are likely to die, nor with false assurance of salvation without regeneration.
items.quote: do not flatter them with vain hopes of life when they are more likely to dye: 2. That you do not flatter them with false perswasions that their state is safe when they are yet unsanctified

items.text: Suit your counsel and prayers to the spiritual state of the sick, giving to the ungodly what is needful for conversion without overwhelming them, yet omitting nothing necessary to salvation.
items.quote: In suiting your counsel, and speeches, and prayers to their state; and not using the same words to the ungodly▪ as you would to the godly.

items.text: Make known to the sick the danger of their disease so that they may prepare for death, yet temper the news so as not to kill them with fear; do not hide the danger when it is great.
items.quote: their disease is so dangerous as calleth for their speedy and serious preparation for death: which will not be lost if God restore them

items.text: Tell the unregenerate sick person plainly of his sin and misery and the necessity of regeneration, even if it offends; to hide it is cruelty that sends him to hell.
items.quote: ordinarily it is a duty to acquaint the sick person that is yet in his sin and unregenerate state, with the truth of his danger, and the necessity of renovation

items.text: When you tell the sick sinner of his danger, also acquaint him with the remedy in Christ, that he may not despair but believe and repent.
items.quote: He must know his sin and misery, or else he is never like to scape it: But he must also be acquainted with the true remedy; and that is your way to keep him from despair

items.text: While there is life, use your utmost skill and diligence to bring the dying sinner to repentance and faith, though the time be short.
items.quote: while there is life, there is some hope: And while there is any hope, we should do our best, when it is for the saving of a soul

items.text: When you are uncertain whether the sick person is truly converted, speak with conditions and suppositions, mixing counsel and comfort according to the grounds of hope or fear.
items.quote: your speech must be mixt and tempered, and your counsels or comforts given with the Conditions and Suppositions exprest.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 29 · Directions for the Aged (and weak). · § 5 … § 12

items.text: Instruct your children and young women from your experience: teach them to be sober, to love their husbands and children, and to obey; tell them the wonders of God's works.
items.quote: Fathers should tell the wonders of his works and mercies to their children

items.text: Be an example of wisdom, gravity, and holiness to your children, showing yourselves such as you would have them become.
items.quote: Such as you would have your Children after you to be, such shew your selves to them in all your Conversation.

items.text: Repress the contentious and censorious spirit of younger believers; call them to unity, charity, and peace.
items.quote: It belongeth to your gravity and experience, to call them unto Unity, Charity and Peace

items.text: Warn the young to beware of covetousness and of being ensnared by the world.
items.quote: give warning to the younger sort, to take heed of Covetousness, and of being ensnared by the world

items.text: Be patient under your infirmities, and do not grow peevish or froward toward those about you.
items.quote: Be patient under all the infirmities and inconveniences of old age... nor grow pievish and froward to those about you.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 29 · Directions for the Aged (and weak). … § 4

items.text: Bless your grandchildren as Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, commending them to God's keeping and redemption.
items.quote: The God which fed me all my life long unto this day, The Angel which Redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads.

items.text: Ask them searching questions about death, judgment, and eternity to engage their consciences and lead them to self-examination.
items.quote: Some pertinent Questions which by the answer will engage them to teach themselves or to judge themselves

items.text: Have them memorize and repeat a plain text of Scripture for every great duty and against every great sin.
items.quote: Cause them to learn some one most plain and pertinent text, for every great and necessary duty, and against every great and dangerous sin

items.text: After convincing them of a duty, press them to a resolution and promise of amendment, with the cautions given.
items.quote: Drive all your Convictions to a Resolution of Endeavour and amendment, and make them sometime promise you to do that which you have convinced them of

items.text: Teach them how to pray, and hear them pray sometime to know their spirit and progress.
items.quote: Teach them how to pray ... and hear them pray sometime

items.text: Provide them suitable books, require them to read alone, and ask what they understand and remember.
items.quote: Put such Books into their hands as are meetest for them, and engage them to read them when they are alone: And ask them what they understand and remember of them

items.text: Do not overwork them; allow them time from work to read and improve their souls.
items.quote: hold them not without necessity so hard to work, as to allow them no time for reading by themselves

items.text: Have them teach one another, with the better readers instructing the rest.
items.quote: Cause them to teach one another when they are together. Let their talk be profitable.

items.text: Do not tire them with too much at once, but give instruction as they are able to receive it.
items.quote: Tire them not out with too much at once; but give it them as they can receive it

items.text: Make instruction sweet and pleasant, mixing in profitable histories such as the Book of Martyrs.
items.quote: Labour to make all sweet and pleasant to them: and to that end sometime mix the reading of some profitable history

items.text: Be kind to your children when they do well, and entice them with kindnesses and rewards.
items.quote: Entice them with kindnesses and rewards: Be kind to your Children when they do well

items.text: Be liberal to your servants as your condition allows, and reward them to make your instruction acceptable.
items.quote: be as liberal to your servants as your Condition will allow you ... A small gift now and then, might signifie much to the further benefit of their souls.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 31 · Directions to the Friends of the Sick that are about them. · § 13 … § 17

items.text: Grieve moderately at the death of relations: neither be insensible nor excessively dejected.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 16
items.quote: To make light of the Death of Relations and friends, be they good or bad, is a sign of a very vitious nature

items.text: Do not be secretly glad at a parent's death for the sake of inheritance or freedom; abhor such selfishness.
items.citation: Baxter, Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 17
items.quote: especially abhor that nature that secretly is glad of the death of Parents, (or little sorrowful) because that their estates are faln to you

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 30 · Directions for the Sick. · Tit. 4. Directions for doing Good to others in our Sickness.

items.text: In sickness, show patience and speak good of God, not a repining word, so that those around you may see faith.
items.quote: Speak good of God... Speak not a repining word against him

items.text: Let those around you see by your confidence and joy that you take heaven for a real felicity, and show them the blessedness of the righteous so they may desire it.
items.quote: Let those that are about you see, that you take the life to come for a reality... Shew them the difference between the death of the righteous and of the wicked.

items.text: Tell those around you of the vanity of the world and the deceitfulness of sin, urging them not to love the world or make light of sin.
items.quote: Now tell poor sinners of the vanity of the world, and of all its glory, wealth and pleasure; and of the mischief and deceitfulness of sin.

items.text: Tell those around you of the excellency and necessity of the love of God, of Christ, and of a holy life, and that without holiness none shall see God.
items.quote: Tell those about you of the Excellency and Necessity of the Love of God, of Heaven, of Christ, and of a holy life.

items.text: Make clear to those around you the difference between the godly and the wicked: the godly choose eternal joys, but the wicked lose their souls for passing pleasure.
items.quote: Endeavour also to make men know the difference between the godly and the wicked.

items.text: Convince those around you of the preciousness of time and the folly of delaying repentance, urging them to secure salvation before it is too late.
items.quote: Labour also to convince men of the pretiousness of Time, and the folly of putting off Repentance and a holy life till the last.

items.text: Make those around you understand the sinfulness of sloth in the matters of God and salvation, and stir them to seek salvation with all diligence.
items.quote: make them understand the sinfulness of sloth... and stir them up to do it with all their might

items.text: Fortify your friends against all fears of suffering for Christ and against impatience in affliction, showing that present sufferings are short and not to be compared with eternal things.
items.quote: Labour also to fortifie the minds of your friends, against all fears of suffering for Christ, and all impatience in any of their afflictions.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 31 · Directions to the Friends of the Sick that are about them. · § 18 … § 19

items.text: Do not let grief for them become sin, unfitting you for duties of joy, thanksgiving, and service to God.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: excess of sorrow is your sin... unfitteth you for many duties

items.text: Trust God's wisdom in their death; do not grudge at his disposal or let your will rise against his.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: what doth your Will but rise up against the will of God; as if you grudged at the exercise of his Dominion

items.text: If they died in faith, rejoice with them in their heavenly joy, and do not mourn as those without hope.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: Love should teach you to rejoice with them that rejoice, and not to mourn as those that have no hope.

items.text: Be thankful that God took them away from the evil to come, which you cannot foresee.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: You know not what mercy God shewed to your friends, in taking them away from the evil to come

items.text: Rejoice that they have entered into immortality, where they die no more.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: you should rejoice that they are arrived at the state of Immortality, where they must Live indeed and die no more

items.text: Remember that you will soon be with them again; let that hope temper your sorrow.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 18
items.quote: Remember how quickly you must be with them again.

items.text: For one who died impenitent, grieve their misery, but not so as to lose your greater joys or neglect your greater duties.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 19
items.quote: Their misery must be your grief: But not such a grief as shall deprive you of your greater Joyes, or disable you for your greater duties.

items.text: For one who died impenitent, do not question God's justice or think yourself more merciful than He.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 19
items.quote: you must neither pretend to be more merciful than he, nor to reprehend his Justice

items.text: Be thankful that you yourself have been delivered from eternal flames, even as you sorrow for them.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 19
items.quote: How glad and thankful should you be to think that God hath delivered your selves from those eternal flames?

items.text: Let the blessedness and glory of God outweigh your sorrow for the lost.
items.citation: A Christian Directory, Part II, Ch. 31, § 19
items.quote: the thoughts of the Blessedness and Glory of God himself, should over-top all the concernments of the creature with you.

work: A Christian Directory, Part II: Christian Oeconomicks
heading: Chapter 19 · Directions for profitable Hearing the Word Preached. · Tit. 1. Directions for the Understanding the Word which you hear.

items.text: Ask your master to resolve your doubts about the Word you hear.
items.quote: servants, that never come to ask the resolution of one doubt... though they have Pastors or Masters that have ability... and willingness to help them.
